SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r1.claim: نؤمن takes لام rather than باء either in the sense ‘believe for the sake of your claim’ or by including acknowledgment of what you claimed.
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r1.anchor: إنما تعدى باللام دون الباء لأحد وجهين

SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r2.claim: The second explanation includes الإقرار: ‘we will not acknowledge to you what you claimed.’
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r2.anchor: وإما أن يضمن معنى الإقرار، أي: [لن] نقر لك بما ادعيته

SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r3.claim: Abū ʿAmr assimilates the nūn into the lām because the sounds are close.
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو بإدغام النون في اللام لتقاربهما

SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r4.claim: One analysis makes جهرة a verbal noun with an omitted verb of the same root: جهرتم جهرة.
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r4.anchor: ناصبها محذوف، وهو من لفظها، تقديره: جهرتم جهرة

SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r5.claim: Another source analysis treats جهرة as a kind of seeing, accusative like القرفصاء after قعد; al-Zamakhsharī begins with it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r5.anchor: مصدر من نوع الفعل فتنتصب انتصاب القرفصاء

SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r6.claim: As a circumstantial accusative, جهرة may describe the subject of نرى: seeing God openly.
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r6.anchor: حال من فاعل " نرى " أي: ذوي جهرة

SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r7.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r7.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ makes جهرة circumstantial to the subject of قلتم: they said it openly.
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r7.anchor: حال من فاعل " قلتم " ، أي: قلتم ذلك مجاهرين

SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r8.claim: This does not require fronting and postponement; the object of saying precedes a circumstantial phrase as in ضربت هندا قائما.
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r8.anchor: ومثل هذا لا يقال فيه تقديم وتأخير، بل أتى بمفعول القول

SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r9.claim: Another circumstantial analysis makes جهرة describe God as seen, manifest and uncovered.
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r9.anchor: حال من اسم الله تعالى، أي: نراه ظاهرا غير مستور

SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya reports making جهرة circumstantial to the subject of نؤمن, but al-Samīn says it has no sensible meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r10.anchor: حال من فاعل " نؤمن " نقله ابن عطية، ولا معنى له

SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r11.claim: Of the six analyses of جهرة, al-Samīn prefers the second: a verbal noun denoting a kind of seeing.
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r11.anchor: والصحيح من هذه الأقوال الستة الثاني

SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads جهرة with fatḥa on hāʾ; it may be a dialect form or a plural of جاهر, supporting a circumstantial reading with نرى.
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r12.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس " جهرة " بفتح الهاء وفيها قولان

SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r13.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says Basrans attest the dialectal fatḥa after an open vowel before a guttural; Kufans allow it without attestation.
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r13.anchor: وهي لغة مسموعة عند البصريين فيما فيه حرف الحلق

SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r14.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r14.claim: The plural reading means seeing God while disclosing the matter and supports making جهرة circumstantial to the subject of نرى.
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r14.anchor: حتى نرى الله كاشفين هذا الأمر، وهي تؤيد كون " جهرة " حالا

SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r15.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r15.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r15.claim: جهر is the opposite of secrecy and means disclosure or appearance; جهر بالقراءة means reciting aloud.
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r15.anchor: والجهر: ضد السر وهو الكشف والظهور، ومنه جهر بالقراءة

SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r16.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r16.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r16.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī likens seeing with the eye to overt action and seeing with the heart to a secret one.
SAMIN-DURR:2:55/r16.anchor: كأن الذي يرى بالعين جاهر بالرؤية، والذي يرى بالقلب مخافت بها

ZAJJAJ:v1p137/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p137/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p137/r1.claim: Jahratan means openly, with nothing hidden from view; the same usage describes openly committing sins without concealment.
ZAJJAJ:v1p137/r1.anchor: معنى (جهرة) غير مستتر عنا بشيء، يقال فلان يجاهر بالمعاصي أي لا يستتر

ZAJJAJ:v1p137/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p137/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p137/r2.claim: The ṣāʿiqa is what strikes people dead, and the Israelites died when it struck them.
ZAJJAJ:v1p137/r2.anchor: وقوله: (فأخذتكم الصاعقة) معنى الصاعقة ما يصعقون منه، أي يموتون، فأخذتهم الصاعقة فماتوا.

ZAJJAJ:v1p137/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p137/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p137/r3.claim: The next verse’s statement that God raised them after their death proves the ṣāʿiqa killed them.
ZAJJAJ:v1p137/r3.anchor: الدليل على أنهم ماتوا قوله عز وجل: (ثم بعثناكم من بعد موتكم لعلكم تشكرون (56).

ZAJJAJ:v1p137/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p137/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p137/r4.claim: This worldly resurrection is likened to the man revived after a century and the people God told to die and then restored.
ZAJJAJ:v1p137/r4.anchor: مثل قوله تعالى: (فأماته الله مائة عام ثم بعثه). ومثل قوله عز وجل: (فقال لهم الله موتوا ثم أحيأهم)

ZAJJAJ:v1p137/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p137/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p137/r5.claim: Scripturally corroborated reports of resurrection answer Arab polytheists who doubted resurrection and support Muhammad’s mission among Jews, Christians, and other scriptural communities.
ZAJJAJ:v1p137/r5.anchor: فأتى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بالأخبار عمن بعث بعد الموت في الدنيا مما توافقه عليه اليهود

ASAD-NOTES:2:55#n40/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:55#n40/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:55#n40/r1.claim: The Qur’an does not specify the form of the punishment; lexicographers differ on the word’s interpretation but agree it conveys vehemence and suddenness.
ASAD-NOTES:2:55#n40/r1.anchor: The lexicographers give various interpretations to this word, but all agree on the element of vehemence and suddenness inherent in it

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p383/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p383/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p383/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr tilts the hamza’s fatḥa toward yā to incline the alif, while leaving rāʾ open when it does not precede the tilted alif.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p383/r1.anchor: فأمال الفتحة التي على الهمزة من رأى نحو الياء، لتميل الألف بإمالة الفتحة نحو الياء، وترك الراء مفتوحة

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p383/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p383/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p383/r2.claim: An open rāʾ does not block imāla here; open emphatic consonants likewise permit it, as in saqā and ṣafā.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p383/r2.anchor: فالقول إن فتح الراء هنا لا يمنع الإمالة

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p383/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p383/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p383/r3.claim: When liaison drops the alif before a following consonant, the standard report leaves rāʾ without imāla in 2:55 and the cited parallels.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p383/r3.anchor: فإذا سقطت الياء في الوصل لساكن لقيها لم يمل الراء، كقوله تعالى: حتى نرى الله جهرة

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p383/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p383/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p383/r4.claim: Arabic has two treatments after liaison elides the alif: restore the fatḥa because its target is gone, or retain imāla because the elision is temporary; Sibawayh supports the first.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p383/r4.anchor: أحدهما ألا يميلوا بالفتحة نحو الكسرة، لأن إمالتها إنما كانت لتميل الألف

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p383/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p383/r5.speaker: أحمد بن موسى
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p383/r5.claim: Ibn Mūsā transmits from ʿAbd al-Wārith and ʿAbbās that Abū ʿAmr used imāla whether or not a consonant followed; Aḥmad says the known reading leaves it uninclined here.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p383/r5.anchor: روى عبد الوارث، وعباس بن الفضل عن أبي عمرو إمالة ذلك كله، استقبله ساكن أو لم يستقبله

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p383/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p383/r6.speaker: أبو الحسن
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p383/r6.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan describes both treatments as available, including retaining imāla after the alif drops.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p383/r6.anchor: إن شئت تركت الإمالة على حالها

NASHR:v2p77/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p77/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p77/r1.claim: The author argues that the alif heard at pause on a tanwīn form is the first alif, derived from yāʾ; the second is a substitute for tanwīn, not the basis for imāla.
NASHR:v2p77/r1.anchor: أن الموقوف عليه من إحدى الألفين هي الأولى المنقلبة عن الياء دون الثانية المبدلة من التنوين

NASHR:v2p77/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p77/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p77/r2.claim: Reports from al-Farrāʾ and al-Akhfash describe pausing on accusative tanwīn without compensation, but the author treats this as a grammatical dispute without qirāʾāt practice.
NASHR:v2p77/r2.anchor: حكى ذلك سماعا منهم الفراء والأخفش

NASHR:v2p77/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p77/r3.speaker: الداني
NASHR:v2p77/r3.claim: Al-Sūsī has a connected-reading imāla of the rāʾ in نرى الله through several transmitters; al-Dānī chose it because it is established by both explicit transmission and performance, including reports from Abū ʿAmr.
NASHR:v2p77/r3.anchor: واختار الإمالة لأنه قد جاء بها نصا وأداء عن أبي شعيب أبو العباس محمود بن محمد الأديب

NASHR:v2p214/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p214/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p214/r1.claim: The author refers back to al-Sūsī’s imāla of the rāʾ in نرى الله and to previously discussed treatments of the following divine-name lām.
NASHR:v2p214/r1.anchor: وتقدم مذهب السوسي في إمالة راء نرى الله آخر باب الإمالة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p46/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p46/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p46/r1.claim: Qatada says the thunderbolt killed them, then God resurrected them so they could complete the remainder of their lifespans.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p46/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ فأخذتكم الصاعقة وأنتم تنظرون ثم بعثناكم من بعد موتكم ﴾ قال أخذتهم الصاعقة أي ماتوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p330/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p330/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p330/r5.claim: Ḥattā often marks a limit and can be causal; Hudhayl substitutes ʿayn for its ḥāʾ, and slight imāla is also heard.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p330/r5.anchor: حتى: حرف معناه الكثير، فيه الغاية، وتكون للتعليل، وإبدال حائها عينا لغة هذيل، وسمع فيها الإمالة قليلا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p330/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p330/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p330/r6.claim: In the sense “see,” the hamza of raʾā drops in several imperfect and imperative forms; it remains in related nouns, and the verb’s forms differ if it means injuring someone’s lung.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p330/r6.anchor: الرؤية الإبصار، والماضي رأى، عينه همزة تحذف في مضارعه، والأمر منه وبناء أفعل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p330/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p330/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p330/r7.claim: The verb meaning “strike his lung” keeps the hamza, unlike “see”; Tamīm also retains hamza in forms other dialects reduce, as shown by a poet’s يرأى.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p330/r7.anchor: فإن كانت رأى بمعنى أصاب رئته، فلا تحذف الهمزة، بل تقول: رآه يرآه: أي أصاب رئته،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p330/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p330/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p330/r8.claim: Al-jahrah means openly or publicly, from j-h-r, the opposite of secrecy; the pattern’s fatḥa is attested by Basrans and analogical for Kufans.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p330/r8.anchor: الجهرة: العلانية، ومنه الجهر: ضد السر، وفتح عين هذا النحو مسموع عند البصريين، مقيس عند الكوفيين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p331/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p331/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p331/r1.claim: Jahara can mean disclose or expose; the related verb also describes clearing a well of mud and revealing its water, illustrated by a poem.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p331/r1.anchor: وجهرت الركية: أخرجت ما فيها من الحمأة وأظهرت الماء،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p331/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p331/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p331/r2.claim: Related forms mean loud-voiced or bright-faced; ajhar means blind, named by antithesis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p331/r2.anchor: والجمهوري: العالي الصوت، وصوت جهير: عال، ووجه جهير: ظاهر الوضاءة، والأجهر: الأعمى، سمي على الضد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p339/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p339/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p339/r7.claim: This is Israel's dialogue with Moses, following his conversation with them in the preceding verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p339/r7.anchor: وإذ قلتم يا موسى: هذه محاورة بني إسرائيل لموسى، وذلك بعد محاورته لهم في الآية قبل هذا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p339/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p339/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p339/r8.claim: Ibn Masud and Qatada say the pronoun addresses the seventy men selected by Moses; their selection is discussed under al-Aʿraf.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p339/r8.anchor: والضمير في قلتم قيل للسبعين المختارين، قاله ابن مسعود وقتادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd says the pronoun addresses all Israelites except those God protected.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r1.anchor: وقيل: الضمير لسائر بني إسرائيل إلا من عصمه الله، قاله ابن زيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r2.claim: A further view identifies the speakers as those who separated from the others with Aaron and did not worship the calf.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r2.anchor: وقيل: الذين انفردوا مع هارون ولم يعبدوا العجل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r3.claim: Some exegetes claim unanimity that the struck people were Moses' seventy selected companions, but he says that conflicts with the disagreement over who said the demand; shifting address is unlikely here.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r3.anchor: تظافرت أقوال أئمة التفسير على أن الذين أصابتهم الصاعقة هم السبعون رجلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r4.claim: Calling their prophet by his name without an honorific is discourteous; their repeated habit contrasts with this community's instruction not to address the Messenger as one another.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r4.anchor: وفي نداء بني إسرائيل لنبيهم باسمه سوء أدب منهم معه، إذ لم يقولوا: يا نبي الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r5.claim: One reading means they would not trust what Moses brought in the Torah, rather than denying faith in Moses personally; لك rather than بك supports this distinction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r5.anchor: قيل معناه: لن نصدقك فيما جئت به من التوراة، ولم يريدوا نفي الإيمان به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r6.claim: Another reading takes faith to mean acknowledgment: they would not acknowledge to Moses that the Torah came from God, with الإيمان used for confession and governed by لام.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r6.anchor: وقيل معناه: لن نقر لك، فعبر عن الإقرار بالإيمان وعداه باللام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r7.claim: The لام may be causal: they would not believe because Moses asserted the Torah.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r7.anchor: وقيل: يجوز أن تكون اللام للعلة، أي لن نؤمن لأجل قولك بالتوراة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r8.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r8.claim: A further interpretation takes the negation as denying complete faith, analogous to the Prophetic statement that a servant does not fully believe until the Prophet is dearer than everyone else.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r8.anchor: وقيل: يجوز أن يراد نفي الكمال، أي لا يكمل إيماننا لك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r9.claim: The cited hadith defines a threshold of complete faith: the Prophet must be more beloved than one's self, family, and all people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r9.anchor: لا يؤمن عبد حتى أكون أحب إليه من نفسه وأهله والناس أجمعين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r10.claim: حتى marks the endpoint of their continued refusal; the wording implies they would believe if they saw God openly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r10.anchor: حتى: هنا حرف غاية، أخبروا بنفي إيمانهم مستصحبا إلى هذه الغاية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r11.claim: Vision here is visual sight without a veil or barrier, and جهرة clarifies that it is not a dream or inward knowledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r11.anchor: والرؤية هنا: هي البصرية، وهي التي لا حجاب دونها ولا ساتر، وانتصاب جهرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r12.claim: The preferred accusative analysis makes جهرة an adverb of manner or kind governed by the prior verb; alternatives treat it as an elliptical circumstantial accusative, ذوي جهرة, or جاهرين بالرؤية.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p340/r12.anchor: والأصح أن يكون منصوبا بالفعل السابق يعدى إلى النوع، كما تعدى إلى لفظ المصدر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r1.claim: On the second grammatical analysis, جهرة describes the people seeing openly rather than the vision itself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r1.anchor: القول تكون من صفات الرائين، وثم قول ثالث، وهو أن يكون راجعا لمعنى القول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and Abu Ubayda report an interpretation connecting جهرة to the utterance or speakers: the demand was voiced openly rather than concealed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r2.anchor: والقول بأن الجهرة راجع لمعنى القول مروي عن ابن عباس وأبي عبيدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r3.claim: He prefers attaching جهرة to the requested vision, as the eloquent syntax indicates, rather than to the utterance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r3.anchor: والظاهر تعلقه بالرؤية لا بالقول، وهو الذي يقتضيه التركيب الفصيح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وسهل بن شعيب وحميد بن قيس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, Sahl ibn Shuayb, and Humayd ibn Qays read جَهْرَة with a fatḥa on the hāʾ; it can be a verbal noun or a plural meaning people seeing openly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وسهل بن شعيب وحميد بن قيس: جهرة، بفتح الهاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari argues Moses showed that vision is impossible because it entails direction; the Israelites persisted after proof, so the thunderbolt punished them as killing punished calf worshipers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r5.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وفي هذا الكلام دليل على أن موسى عليه السلام رادهم، وعرفهم أن رؤية ما لا يجوز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r6.speaker: القدرية والمعتزلة والنجارية والجهمية والخوارج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r6.claim: The Qadariyya, Muʿtazila, Najjariyya, Jahmiyya, and some Kharijites hold that God cannot be seen.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r6.anchor: ذهبت القدرية والمعتزلة والنجارية والجهمية ومن شاركهم من الخوارج إلى استحالة ذلك في حق الباري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r7.speaker: أكثر المسلمين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r7.claim: Most Muslims affirm that believers will see God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r7.anchor: وذهب أكثر المسلمين إلى إثبات الرؤية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r8.speaker: الكرامية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r8.claim: The Karramiyya say God is seen from above and has a lower direction, and is seen as a body.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r8.anchor: فقال الكرامية: يرى في جهة فوق وله تحت، ويرى جسما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r9.speaker: المشبهة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r9.claim: The anthropomorphists say God is seen in an image.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r10.speaker: أهل السنة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r10.claim: Ahl al-Sunna say believers see God without opposition, facing, location, color, image, form, or corporeality, while knowing He differs from created things.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r10.anchor: بل يراه المؤمنون، يعلمون أنه بخلاف المخلوقات كما علموه كذلك قبل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r11.claim: Sound hadith reports on the vision are abundant, so he affirms it; this difficult theological question is also treated at length by the Imami scholar Abu Jaʿfar al-Tusi.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r11.anchor: وقد استفاضت الأحاديث الصحيحة الثابتة في رؤية الله تعالى، فوجب المصير إليها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r12.claim: The verse does not prove al-Zamakhshari's claim that vision is impossible; he accuses him of loading the wording with his Muʿtazilite doctrine.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p341/r12.anchor: وليس في الآية ما يدل على ما ذهب إليه الزمخشري من استحالة الرؤية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r1.speaker: أكثر المعتزلة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r1.claim: Most Muʿtazilites say God does not see Himself; another Muʿtazilite group says He does, while al-Kaʿbi and al-Najjar say He sees neither Himself nor anything else.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r1.anchor: اختلفوا في رؤية الحق نفسه، فذهب أكثر المعتزلة إلى أنه لا يرى نفسه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r2.claim: أخذ means to seize by hand; here the thunderbolt overtook and encompassed them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r2.anchor: فأخذتكم الصاعقة: أي استولت عليكم وأحاطت بكم. وأصل الأخذ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r3.claim: The commentary lists proposed senses for the thunderbolt: fire from heaven, death, a heavenly host whose sound killed them, prolonged terror, fainting, lethal punishment, or a heavenly cry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r3.anchor: والصاعقة هنا: هل هي نار من السماء أحرقتهم، أو الموت، أو جند سماوي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r4.speaker: المحققون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r4.claim: The soundest view is that the thunderbolt was the cause of death rather than death itself; the commentary cites the parallel wording about the earthquake seizing them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r4.anchor: أقوال، أصحها: أنها سبب الموت، لا الموت،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r5.speaker: المفسرون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r5.claim: Exegetes agree that the interval during which they were dead or thunderstruck lasted a day and a night.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r5.anchor: وأجمع المفسرون على أن المدة من الموت أو الصعق كانت يوما وليلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r6.claim: One report says Moses was struck too; another says he was thunderstruck but did not die, which the author considers correct from the wording أفاق for Moses and بعثناكم for the others.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r6.anchor: وقيل: أصاب موسى ما أصابهم، وقيل صعق ولم يمت، قالوا: وهو الصحيح،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r7.claim: A further view says they fainted like Moses and did not die, since صعق can be used for something other than death; Jarir's verse supplies an example.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r7.anchor: وقيل: غشي عليهم كهو ولم يموتوا، والصعق يطلق على غير الموت، وقال جرير:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r8.speaker: جرير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r8.claim: Jarir's line about al-Farazdaq being struck by the ṣawāʿiq illustrates the word's use for an affliction rather than literal death.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r8.anchor: وقال جرير: وهل كان الفرزدق غير قرد ... أصابته الصواعق فاستدارا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r9.claim: The apparent cause of the thunderbolt was their defiant demand to see God, since they asked for vision only out of obstinacy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r9.anchor: والظاهر أن سبب أخذ الصاعقة إياهم قولهم: لن نؤمن لك حتى نرى الله جهرة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r10.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r10.claim: Other explanations assign the cause to another disbelief in Moses, rejecting his Torah, or worshiping the calf.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r10.anchor: وقيل: سبب أخذ الصعقة إياهم هو غير هذا القول من كفرهم بموسى، أو تكذيبهم إياه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r11.speaker: عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r11.claim: Amr reads الصعقة rather than الصاعقة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r12.claim: Requesting vision in this world is objectionable because vision occurs only in the afterlife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r12.anchor: واستعظم سؤال الرؤية حيث وقع، لأن رؤيته لا تحصل إلا في الآخرة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r13.claim: Another rationale is that seeing God ends a person's legal responsibility, so requesting it amounts to requesting the end of obligation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r13.anchor: أو لأن حكم الله أن يزيل التكليف عن العبد حال ما يراه، فكان طلبها طلبا لإزالة التكليف،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r14.claim: A further rationale is that demanding more proof after the messenger's truth is established is obstinacy, and withholding vision in this world serves an important benefit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r14.anchor: أو لأنه لما دلت الدلائل على صدق المدعي كان طلب الدلائل الزائدة تعنتا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r15.claim: The clause وأنتم تنظرون is circumstantial; its object is the thunderbolt's seizing them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r15.anchor: وأنتم تنظرون: جملة حالية، ومتعلق النظر: أخذ الصعقة إياكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r16.claim: Possible objects of sight include the thunderbolt overtaking them, one another falling dead, the survivors, or the thunderbolt's effects on their bodies after revival.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r16.anchor: أي وأنتم تنظرون إلى ما حل بكم منها أو بعضكم إلى بعض كيف يخر ميتا، أو إلى الأحياء،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r17.claim: نظر may mean knowing that the thunderbolt is taking them, so the wording uses seeing for knowledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r17.anchor: أو تعلمون أنها تأخذكم. فعبر بالنظر عن العلم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r18.claim: Another explanation is that they watched each person come back to life, as in the story of al-ʿUzayr.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p342/r18.anchor: أو ينظر كل منكم إلى إحياء نفسه، كما وقع في قصة العزير،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p349/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p349/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p349/r3.claim: Their demand to see God openly was an improper, obstinate challenge; the thunderbolt followed from that demand.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p349/r3.anchor: ثم التوبيخ لهم بسؤالهم ما كان لا ينبغي لهم أن يسألوه، وهو رؤية الله عيانا، لأنه كان سؤال تعنت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p350/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p350/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p350/r2.claim: God explicitly attributes blessings to Himself but leaves the punishment’s agent unspoken, although it is truly from Him; this passage enumerates blessings, and naming punishment directly could overpower their joy. Encouragement predominates over its warning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p350/r2.anchor: وحيث ذكر النقم لم ينسبها إليه تعالى فقال: فأخذتكم الصاعقة. وسر ذلك أنه موضع تعداد للنعم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r1.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r1.claim: The speakers are the seventy men Moses selected for the appointment concerning the Torah.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r1.anchor: القائل هم السبعون الذي أختارهم موسى عليه السلام لميقات التوراة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r2.claim: One account places their demand after Moses returned, killed the calf worshippers, and burned the calf.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r2.anchor: قيل : قالوه بعد الرجوع وقتل عبدة العجل وتحريق عجلهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r3.claim: Some reports suggest that the speakers were the seventy at a second appointment, when God sent them to apologize for the calf worshippers.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r3.anchor: ويفهم من بعض الآثار أن القائل أهل الميقات الثاني الذي ضربه الله تعالى للإعتذار عن عبدة العجل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r4.claim: Other views identify the speakers as ten thousand of Moses's people, or all Israelites except those God protected.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r4.anchor: وقيل : القائل عشرة آلاف من قومه وقيل : الضمير لسائر بني إسرائيل إلا من عصمه الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r5.claim: Al-Alusi says his later discussion of the episode in Surat al-A'raf will provide relevant material.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r5.anchor: وسيأتي إن شاء الله تعالى في الأعراف ما ينفعك هنا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r6.claim: The lām may mark purpose, or make the clause transitive by implying acknowledgment: Moses is the person acknowledged and the omitted content is that God gave him the Torah or spoke commands to him.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r6.anchor: واللام من ( لك ) إمالام الأجل أو للتعدية بتضمين معنى الأقرار على أن ( موسى ) مقر له

ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r7.claim: They had previously believed in Moses; here they deny a particular belief and acknowledgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r7.anchor: وقد كان هؤلاء مؤمنين من قبل بموسى عليه السلام إلا أنهم نفوا هذا الإيمان المعين والإقرار الخاص

ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r8.claim: Alternatively, they deny the completeness of their faith, as in the Prophetic saying that none truly believes until he loves for his fellow believer what he loves for himself.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r8.anchor: وقيل : أرادوا نفي الكمال أي لا يكمل إيماننا لك كما قيل في قوله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r9.claim: Al-Alusi has not found any major exegete claiming that they had no faith at all.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r9.anchor: والقول إنهم لم يكونوا مؤمنين أصلا لم نره لأحد من ائمة التفسير

ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r10.claim: Here حتى is a particle marking the endpoint.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r11.claim: Jahrah originally describes reciting aloud and is borrowed for direct vision because both involve full, manifest appearance.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r11.anchor: و ( الجهرة ) في الأصل جهرت بالقراءة إذا رفعت صوتك بها واستعيرت للمعاينة بجامع الظهور التام

ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r12.speaker: الرغب
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r12.claim: Al-Raghib defines jahri as something appearing with excessive force to sight or hearing, illustrated by seeing openly and speaking aloud.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r12.anchor: وقال الرغب : الجهري قال لظهور الشيء بإفراط حاسة البصر أو حاسة السمع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r13.claim: Jahrah may be an emphatic verbal noun excluding dream or inward knowledge as the intended vision, or a circumstantial accusative describing either the vision or the seers.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r13.anchor: وانتصابها على أنها مصدر مؤكد مزيل لإحتمال أن تكون الرؤية مناما أو علما بالقلب وقيل : على أنها حال

ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r14.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو عبيدة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r14.claim: A third interpretation makes jahrah describe the speech or speakers: they voiced the demand openly, without hesitation or concern.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r14.anchor: وهو المروي عن إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما وأبي عبيدة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r15.speaker: سهل بن شعيب وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r15.claim: Sahl ibn Shu'ayb and others read jahrah with fatḥa on the hāʾ; it can be a verbal noun like ghalabah or a plural of jāhir, with circumstantial syntax in the latter analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r15.anchor: وقرأ سهل بن شعيب وغيره ( جهرة ) بفتح الهاء وهي إما مصدر كالغلبة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r16.claim: The verb means that the thunderbolt seized, overcame, and surrounded them; its basic sense is grasping by hand.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r16.anchor: أي أستولت عليكم وأحاطت بكم واصلال أخذ القبض باليد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r17.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r17.claim: The thunderbolt is variously explained as fire from heaven that burned them, a heavenly host whose sound killed them, or a heavenly cry that felled them dead for a day and night.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r17.anchor: نار من السماء أحرقتهم أو جند سماوي سمعوا حسهم فماتوا أو صيحة سماوية خروا لها صعقين ميتين يوما وليلة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r18.claim: Al-Alusi's sounder view is that Moses was struck unconscious but did not die, unlike the others; the text says he recovered while they were raised again.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r18.anchor: والصحيح لا وأنه صعق ولم يمت لظاهر ثم أفاق في حقه و ( ثم بعثناكم ) إلخ في حقهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r19.speaker: عمر وعلي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r19.claim: Umar and Ali read الصعقة in place of الصاعقة.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r19.anchor: وقرأ عمر وعلي رضي الله تعالى عنهما ( الصعقة )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r20.claim: The clause “while you looked” is circumstantial.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r21.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r21.claim: What they looked at may be the thunderbolt's event, its remaining mark on their bodies after revival, or their individual revival, as in the report that Ezra's limbs were restored one by one.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r21.anchor: ومتعلق النظر ما حل بهم من الصاعقة أو أثرها الباقي في أجسامهم بعد البعث أو إحياء كل منهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r22.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r22.claim: Alternatively, they knew that the thunderbolt would strike them, or they looked at one another.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r22.anchor: والمعنى ( وأنتم ) تعلمون أنها تأخذكم أو و ( أنتم ) يقابل بعضكم بعضا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r23.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r23.claim: Abu Hayyan allows “while you look” to mean that they awaited the requested vision, citing Arabic نظر الرجل for waiting; al-Alusi says this reading is possible but unattested and he cannot affirm it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r23.anchor: قال في البحر : ولو ذهب ذاهب إلى أن المعنى ( وأنتم تنظرون ) إجابة السؤال في حصول الرؤية لكم كان وجها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r24.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r24.claim: The supporting poetic line uses تنظراني to mean “wait for me”; al-Alusi cites it only as a possible Arabic usage, not as an established interpretation here.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p261/r24.anchor: كما قال : فإنكما إن ( تنظراني ) ساعة من الدهر تنفعني لدى أم جندب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p96/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p96/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p96/r1.claim: At God's command Moses selected seventy leading Israelites to seek pardon for calf worship; after fasting and purifying themselves, they went to Sinai and asked to hear God's speech.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p96/r1.anchor: وذلك أن الله تعالى أمر موسى عليه السلام أن يأتيه في ناس من بني إسرائيل يعتذرون إليه من عبادة العجل،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p96/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p96/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p96/r2.claim: A cloud covered Sinai as Moses entered; the people approached and prostrated, were screened from Moses' blinding light, and heard God command worship of Him alone and recount their deliverance from Egypt.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p96/r2.anchor: فلما دنا موسى إلى طور سيناء من الجبل وقع عليه عمود الغمام وتغشى الجبل كله، فدخل في الغمام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p96/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p96/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p96/r3.claim: The people demanded direct sight; because Arabs can use seeing for inward knowledge, jahra clarifies that they meant sight with their eyes.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p96/r3.anchor: معاينة وذلك أن العرب تجعل العلم بالقلب رؤية، فقال جهرة ليعلم أن المراد منه العيان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p96/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p96/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p96/r4.claim: The sa'iqa is interpreted as death, or as fire from heaven that burned them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p96/r4.anchor: أي الموت، وقيل: نار جاءت من السماء فأحرقتهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p96/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p96/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p96/r5.claim: They were looking at one another as death struck; another explanation takes looking to mean knowing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p96/r5.anchor: أي ينظر بعضكم إلى بعض حين أخذكم الموت. وقيل: تعلمون، والنظر يكون بمعنى العلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p96/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p96/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p96/r6.claim: After their death Moses wept and pleaded, quoting his prayer that God not destroy them for the fools' deed; God revived them one by one after a day and night.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p96/r6.anchor: فلم يزل يناشد ربه حتى أحياهم الله تعالى رجلا بعد رجل بعد ما ماتوا يوما وليلة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r1.claim: لَكَ can mean ‘because of what you say’ or simply ‘believe/affirm you.’
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r1.anchor: أي لأجل قولك، أو لن نقر لك

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r2.claim: جهرة originally means reciting aloud and is borrowed for seeing face to face; it is accusative as a verbal noun for a kind of seeing or as a circumstance of the subject or object.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r2.anchor: عيانا وهي في الأصل مصدر قولك

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r3.claim: A variant with fatḥa, جهرة, is either a verbal noun like غلبة or a plural like كتبة meaning ‘those who disclose’; in the latter analysis it must be a circumstantial accusative of the subject.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r3.anchor: وقرىء جهرة بالفتح على أنها مصدر كالغلبة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r4.claim: The questioners were the seventy men Moses selected for the appointment; another report says ten thousand of his people.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r5.claim: Their requested belief concerned either God, who gave Moses the Torah and spoke to him, or Moses’s claim to prophethood.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r5.anchor: والمؤمن به: إن الله الذي أعطاك التوراة وكلمك

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r6.claim: The affliction followed obstinate insistence on an impossible demand based on imagining God as a body in a direction and place; such bodily sight is impossible. Sight without modality is possible for believers in the afterlife and for some prophets at times in this life.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r6.anchor: فإنهم ظنوا أنه تعالى يشبه الأجسام فطلبوا رؤيته رؤية الأجسام في الجهات والأحياز المقابلة للرائي

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r7.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r7.claim: One account says a fire came down from heaven and burned them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r7.anchor: قيل جاءت نار من السماء فأحرقتهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r8.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r8.claim: Another account identifies the صاعقة as a cry.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r9.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r9.claim: A further account says troops were heard hissing, whereupon the people fell dead or senseless for a day and night.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55/r9.anchor: وقيل جنود سمعوا بحسيسها فخروا صعقين ميتين يوما وليلة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:55#2/r1.claim: They witnessed either the affliction itself or its effects.

BURSEVI:v1p110/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p110/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p110/r2.claim: The verse recalls the seventy Israelite elders Moses chose to accompany him to the mountain to apologize for worship of the calf; they were not the first group of seventy chosen after Pharaoh drowned.
BURSEVI:v1p110/r2.anchor: السبعين من أسلافكم الذين اختارهم موسى حين ذهبوا معه إلى الطور للاعتذار عن عبادة العجل

BURSEVI:v1p110/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p110/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p110/r3.claim: They refused to accept Moses’ claim that the book was from God, that he had heard God speak, and that God commanded them to accept and follow it until they saw God.
BURSEVI:v1p110/r3.anchor: لن نصدقك لأجل قولك ودعوتك على أن هذا كتاب الله وأنك سمعت كلامه وأن الله تعالى أمرنا بقبوله والعمل به

BURSEVI:v1p110/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p110/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p110/r4.claim: Jahra means seeing God openly, face to face, without a barrier, with the clarity associated with an audible utterance.
BURSEVI:v1p110/r4.anchor: لا ساتر بيننا وبينه كالجهر في الوضوح والانكشاف لأن الجهر في المسموعات والمعاينة في المبصرات

BURSEVI:v1p110/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p110/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p110/r5.claim: Jahra is accusative as a verbal noun describing a kind of seeing, or as a circumstantial accusative modifying either the seers or God as the seen.
BURSEVI:v1p110/r5.anchor: ونصبها عن المصدرية لأنها نوع من الرؤية فكأنها مصدر الفعل الناصب أو حال من الفاعل

BURSEVI:v1p110/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p110/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p110/r6.claim: The saʿiqa is a burning fire with a sound descending from the sky, or any terrifying event that kills or removes reason; it can be sound, fire, or another form.
BURSEVI:v1p110/r6.anchor: هي نار محرقة فيها صوت نازلة من السماء وهي كل أمر مهول مميت أو مزيل للعقل والفهم

BURSEVI:v1p110/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p110/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p110/r7.claim: They were struck for stubbornly demanding an impossible earthly vision of God; vision without modality is possible for believers in the afterlife and for select prophets in some worldly states.
BURSEVI:v1p110/r7.anchor: وإنما أحرقتهم الصاعقة لسؤالهم ما هو مستحيل على الله في الدنيا ولفرط العناد والتعنت

BURSEVI:v1p110/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p110/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p110/r8.claim: They saw the descending lightning or fire; if it was a terrifying sound, some died first and the others saw that they had died, figuratively called seeing death.
BURSEVI:v1p110/r8.anchor: فقد مات بعضهم أولا ورأى السابقون أنهم ماتوا ويسمى هذا رؤية الموت مجازا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p134/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p134/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p134/r19.claim: After clinging to the sensory calf, the Israelites demanded sensory sight of their Creator, forgetting His favors and signs; their story consoles Muhammad over his people’s rejection.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p134/r19.anchor: ولما استتيبوا عن عبادة العجل التي تقيدوا فيها بالمحسوس الذي هو مثل في الغباوة طلبوا رؤية بارئهم بالحس

BIQAI-FULL:v1p134/r20.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p134/r20.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p134/r20.claim: Their demand came despite clear signs that should remove doubt; it reflects a rigid attachment to imagination and sense, a pattern also seen in Moses’ own people.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p134/r20.anchor: والحال أن الفرقان الذي لا يدع شبهة ولا يبقى حيرة قائم بين أيديهم , لأنهم من الجمود والوقوف مع الوهم والحس بمكان عظيم ,

BIQAI-FULL:v1p134/r21.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p134/r21.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p134/r21.claim: Calling Moses by his bare name, despite witnessing God honor him and honor them through him, shows their discourtesy and harshness.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p134/r21.anchor: فدعوتموه باسمه جفاء وغلظة كما يدعو بعضكم بعضا ولم تخصوه بما يدل على تعظيمه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r1.claim: Biqai points to 9:61 as a Qur’anic parallel where the lām construction “believe for the believers” differs from “believe in God.”

BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r2.claim: This distinction explains that the Israelites accepted Moses’ basic message but stopped short of accepting the detailed matters he brought.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r3.claim: The particle ḥattā marks a bounded endpoint that falls within the preceding condition’s scope, unlike the purposive particle kay.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r3.anchor: { حتى } كلمة تفهم غاية محوطة يدخل ما بعدها في حكم ما قبلها مقابل معنى لكي

BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r4.claim: Seeing is access to an inward reality through its visible outward aspect; dream vision presents inner realities in forms like waking sight.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r4.anchor: { نرى } من الرؤية وهي اطلاع على باطن الشيء الذي أظهر منه مبصره الذي أظهره منه منظره

BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r5.claim: The name Allah here carries the sense of divine greatness, heightening the impropriety of their demand.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r5.anchor: { الله } أي مع ما له من العظمة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r6.claim: Al-Harali defines jahr as public disclosure reaching notoriety and an audience not specifically selected, in contrast to a private communication for its intended recipient.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r6.anchor: قال الحرالي : من الجهر وهو الإعلان بالشيء إلى حد الشهرة وبلاغه لمن لا يقصد في مقابلة السر المختص بمن يقصد به

BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r7.claim: Public sight of God is an unsuitable demand: unveiling belongs to chosen people granted nearness, not those in a position of distance and rejection.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r7.anchor: وهذا المطلوب مما لا يليق بالجهر لتحقيق اختصاصه بمن يكشف له الحجاب من خاصة من يجوزه القرب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r8.claim: The passage points to Moses’ request to see God and to the radiant faces looking toward their Lord as scriptural language for this special vision.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136/r8.anchor: وفيه شهادة بتبلدهم عن موقع الرؤية , فإن موسى عليه السلام قال

BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r1.claim: The Prophet says that believers will see their Lord, a report Biqāʿī uses to explain the verse’s language of vision.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r1.anchor: وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( إنكم ترون ربكم ) فالاسم المذكور

BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r2.claim: Biqāʿī says the verse uses “Lord” for vision because the name Allah connotes the unseen and is associated here with loss rather than attainment.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r2.anchor: فالاسم المذكور لمعنى الرؤية إنما هو الرب لما في اسم الله تعالى من الغيب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r3.claim: He glosses taking as grasping an entire thing with force and violence.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r3.anchor: من الأخذ وهو تناول الشيء بجملته بنوع بطش وقوة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r4.claim: One unnamed reported view interprets the thunderbolt as a cry.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r4.anchor: أي لقولكم هذا لما فيه من الفظاعة وانتهاك الحرمة , { الصاعقة } قيل : هي صيحة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r5.claim: Another view makes it fire descending from heaven and burning them; Biqāʿī favors it because the verse says they were watching.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r5.anchor: قيل : نار نزلت من السماء فأحرقتهم , ويؤيده قوله { وأنتم تنظرون

BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r6.claim: They were killed for demanding vision in a manner resembling the calf worshippers, whom God had also killed.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r6.anchor: لأنكم كنتم في طلبكم رؤيته على ضرب من حال عبدة العجل , فأماتكم كما أماتهم بالقتل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r14.claim: Together with the earlier warning that no soul can avail another, this account warns Arabs who deny resurrection and directs them to ask the People of the Book about their ancestors’ revival and other resurrection stories.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p136#2/r14.anchor: وفي هذه الآية وما تقدمها من آية { واتقوا يوما لا تجزي نفس } تنبيه للعرب

DURR-FULL:v1p169/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p169/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p169/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses “openly” as “in the open.”
DURR-FULL:v1p169/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {حتى نرى الله جهرة} قال: علانية

DURR-FULL:v1p169/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p169/r6.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
DURR-FULL:v1p169/r6.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas identifies them as the seventy chosen by Moses; the thunderbolt killed them, and they were revived to complete their lifespans.
DURR-FULL:v1p169/r6.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس في قوله {وإذ قلتم يا موسى لن نؤمن لك حتى نرى الله جهرة} قال: هم السبعون الذي اختارهم موسى

DURR-FULL:v1p169/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p169/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p169/r7.claim: Qatada says God punished the people by killing them and revived them so they could live out the rest of their appointed terms.
DURR-FULL:v1p169/r7.anchor: عن قتادة في الآية قال: عوقب القوم فأماتهم الله عقوبة ثم بعثهم إلى بقية آجالهم

DURR-FULL:v1p169/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p169/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p169/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses al-sāʿiqa as punishment, whose original sense is death; he cites Rabi'a's verse about fearing a deadly calamity as Arabic usage.
DURR-FULL:v1p169/r8.anchor: أما سمعت ربيعة وهو يقول: وقد كنت أخشى عليك الحتوف وقد كنت آمنك الصاعقة

IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains jahra as openly, meaning that they demanded to see God.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس انه قال في قول الله : لن نؤمن لك حتى نرى الله جهرة : اي علانية ، اي حتى نرى الله

IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r2.claim: Qatadah glosses jahra as seeing God directly; Abu Muhammad says al-Rabi ibn Anas gave the same gloss.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قول الله تعالى : واذ قلتم يا موسى لن نؤمن لك حتى نرى الله جهرة اي عيانا . قال أبو محمد : وكذا فسره الربيع بن انس

IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r3.speaker: عدوة بن رويم
IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r3.claim: Urwa ibn Ruwaym recounts that after Israel refused Moses' warning, some were struck down while others watched; the first group was revived, then the others were struck down and revived. A second version varies the sequence.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r3.anchor: قال سمعت عدوة بن رويم يقول سال بنو اسرائيل موسى فقالوا : لن نؤمن لك حتى نرى الله جهرة ، فاخبرهم انهم لن يطيقوا ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r4.claim: Qatadah says the thunderbolt seized them by killing them.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : فاخذتكم الصاعقة وأنتم تنظرون قال : اخذتهم الصاعقة اي ماتوا

IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r5.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r5.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas identifies the group as the seventy men Moses selected; they heard a sound, fell unconscious, and died.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r5.anchor: عن الربيع بن انس في قوله : فاخذتكم الصاعقة قال : هم السبعون الذين اختارهم موسى فساروا معه

IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r6.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r6.claim: Al-Suddi says the thunderbolt was fire.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r6.anchor: عن السدى : قوله : واذ قلتم يا موسى لن نؤمن لك حتى نرى الله جهرة فاخذتكم الصاعقة والصاعقة نار

IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r7.speaker: مروان بن الحكم
IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r7.claim: Marwan ibn al-Hakam glosses the thunderbolt as a cry from the sky.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p111/r7.anchor: قال رايت مروان بن الحكم على منبر مكة فسمعته يقول وهو يخطب : فاخذتكم الصاعقة

IBNABIHATIM:v1p112/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p112/r1.speaker: عروة بن رويم
IBNABIHATIM:v1p112/r1.claim: Urwa ibn Ruwaym explains “while you looked on” as some being struck down while others watched.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p112/r1.anchor: سمعت عروة بن رويم يقول : وأنتم تنظرون قال فصعق بعضكم وبعض ينظرون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p146/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p146/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p146/r5.claim: Those who said this were the seventy Moses selected; most commentators place their selection after the calf episode to seek forgiveness for Israel, while al-Naqqash and others place it after the sea crossing at the appointed time; Ibn Atiyya prefers the first chronology.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p146/r5.anchor: وقوله تعالى: وإذ قلتم يا موسى يريد السبعين الذين اختارهم موسى، واختلف في وقت اختيارهم.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p146/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p146/r6.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p146/r6.claim: Most commentators place the seventy’s selection after the calf worship so they could seek forgiveness for the Israelites.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p146/r6.anchor: فحكى أكثر المفسرين أن ذلك بعد عبادة العجل، اختارهم ليستغفروا لبني إسرائيل.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p146/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p146/r7.speaker: النقاش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p146/r7.claim: Al-Naqqash and others instead place the selection when Moses left the sea and sought the appointed meeting; Ibn Atiyya prefers the first account.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p146/r7.anchor: وحكى النقاش وغيره أنه اختارهم حين خرج من البحر وطلب بالميعاد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p146/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p146/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p146/r8.claim: The account says some Israelites who had not worshipped the calf asked Moses to hear God; he was told to choose seventy elders but found only sixty, so ten youths were added and became elders overnight. Six per tribe made 72; Joshua and Talut stayed behind with equal reward. Moses took the seventy after three days’ abstinence and bathing, left Aaron in charge, and brought them to the mountain, where cloud and light came over them and they prostrated.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p146/r8.anchor: وقصة السبعين أن موسى صلى الله عليه وسلم لما رجع من تكليم الله ووجد العجل قد عبد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p146/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p146/r9.speaker: النقاش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p146/r9.claim: Al-Naqqash and others say a cloud covered the seventy, light separated them from Moses, and they fell in prostration.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p146/r9.anchor: قال النقاش وغيره: غشيتهم سحابة وحيل بينهم وبين موسى بالنور فوقعوا سجودا.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r1.claim: Al-Suddi and others report that the seventy heard God command and prohibit, could not bear it, and asked Moses to hear and interpret for them; some later altered what they heard, linked to 2:75. Their faith became unsettled and God tested them with a demand to see Him openly. The request was not intrinsically impossible, though Ahl al-Sunna hold seeing God in this world textually impossible; the thunderbolt burned and killed them in deathlike stillness as a warning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r1.anchor: قال السدي وغيره: وسمعوا كلام الله يأمر وينهى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r2.claim: Qatada says they died and their spirits departed, then were restored to complete their lifespans; while they lay motionless Moses pleaded that returning to Israel without them would bring ruin and disbelief, since they had left as the best people. Ibn Atiyya clarifies they were good when they departed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: «ماتوا وذهبت أرواحهم ثم ردوا لاستيفاء آجالهم، فحين حصلوا في ذلك الهمود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r3.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r3.claim: Some say Moses thought the seventy were punished for calf worship; this explains his question in 7:155 about destroying them for what the fools did, meaning the calf worshippers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r3.anchor: وقال قوم: بل ظن موسى عليه السلام أن السبعين إنما عوقبوا بسبب عبادة العجل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r4.speaker: ابن فورك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r4.claim: Ibn Furak suggests the seventy were punished for asking Moses to seek vision for them by saying “show us,” something outside his power.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r4.anchor: وقال ابن فورك: يحتمل أن تكون معاقبة السبعين لإخراجهم طلب الرؤية عن طريقه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r5.claim: Jahratan is a verbal noun used circumstantially; it most apparently attaches to the pronoun in “we see,” though it may attach to “we believe” or “you said.”

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r6.claim: Jahr means openly, opposite to secrecy; jahara al-amr means that a man made a matter manifest.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r6.anchor: والجهرة العلانية، ومنه الجهر ضد السر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r7.speaker: سهل بن شعيب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r7.claim: Sahl ibn Shuʿayb and Humayd ibn Qays read jahratan with fatḥa on hāʾ; Basrans attest this after an open syllable before a guttural, while Kufans allow it without attestation. Ibn Atiyya also suggests it could be the plural of jāhir, “openly as manifest witnesses.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r7.anchor: وقرأ سهل بن شعيب وحميد بن قيس: «جهرة» بفتح الهاء، وهي لغة مسموعة عند البصريين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r8.speaker: عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r8.claim: Umar and Ali read fa-akhadhatkum al-ṣaʿqa; al-ṣaʿqa is what happens to a person from a thunderbolt, discussed earlier in the sura.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147/r8.anchor: وقرأ عمر وعلي رضي الله عنهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147#2/r1.claim: The phrase means they looked at their condition; Ibn Atiyya adds the punishment transformed them and took away their sight.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p147#2/r1.anchor: وتنظرون معناه إلى حالكم. قال القاضي أبو محمد عبد الحق رحمه الله: حتى أحالهم العذاب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p83/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p83/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p83/r1.claim: One view identifies the speakers as the seventy men chosen to accompany Moses.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p83/r1.anchor: في القائلين لموسى ذلك قولان أحدهما أنهم السبعون المختارون قاله ابن مسعود وابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p83/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p83/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p83/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says the speakers were all the Israelites except those God protected; they demanded to see God before accepting Moses’ word.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p83/r2.anchor: والثاني جميع بني اسرائيل إلا من عصم الله منهم قاله ابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p83/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p83/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p83/r3.claim: One interpretation makes jahratan describe their speech: they said the demand openly.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p83/r3.anchor: وفي جهرة قولان أحدهما أنه صفة لقولهم أي جهروا بذلك القول قاله ابن عباس وابوعبيدة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p83/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p83/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p83/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says jahratan means a clear, uncovered vision: ‘show Him to us plainly.’
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p83/r4.anchor: والثاني أنها الرؤية البينة أي ارناه غير مستتر عنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p83/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p83/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p83/r5.claim: Al-ṣāʿiqa is what strikes them down, that is, causes them to die.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p83/r5.anchor: ومعنى الصاعقة ما يصعقون منه أي يموتون ومن الدليل على أنهم ماتوا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r1.claim: God reminds the Israelites of the favor of restoring them after they demanded to see Him openly, something impossible for them and their like.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى: واذكروا نعمتي عليكم في بعثي لكم بعد الصعق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains jahrah as openly or publicly.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن جريج، قال ابن عباس في هذه الآية: {وإذ قلتم يا موسى لن نؤمن لك حتى نرى الله جهرة} قال: علانية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the demand as seeing God openly, that is, seeing God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي الحويرث، عن ابن عباس، أنه قال في قول الله تعالى: {لن نؤمن لك حتى نرى الله جهرة} أي علانية، أي حتى نرى الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r4.speaker: قتادة والربيع بن أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r4.claim: Qatada and al-Rabi ibn Anas explain the demand as seeing God with one’s eyes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة، والربيع بن أنس: {حتى نرى الله جهرة} أي عيانا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r5.speaker: الربيع بن أنس عن أبي جعفر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r5.claim: A report identifies the group as the seventy Moses chose; after hearing speech they demanded to see God, heard a sound and fell dead from the strike.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r5.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر عن الربيع بن أنس: هم السبعون الذين اختارهم موسى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r6.speaker: مروان بن الحكم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r6.claim: Marwan ibn al-Hakam glosses the thunderbolt as a cry from heaven.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r6.anchor: وقال مروان بن الحكم، فيما خطب به على منبر مكة: الصاعقة: صيحة من السماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r7.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r7.claim: Al-Suddi explains the thunderbolt as fire.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r7.anchor: وقال السدي في قوله: {فأخذتكم الصاعقة} الصاعقة: نار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r8.speaker: عروة بن رويم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r8.claim: Urwa ibn Ruwaym says some were struck while others watched; then the first group was revived and the watching group was struck.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r8.anchor: وقال عروة بن رويم في قوله: {وأنتم تنظرون} قال: فصعق بعضهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r9.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r9.claim: Al-Suddi says the seventy died, Moses feared what he would tell Israel, and God revealed that they had worshiped the calf; God restored them one by one, and this revival is the favor recalled in verse 56.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p263#2/r9.anchor: وقال السدي: {فأخذتكم الصاعقة} فماتوا، فقام موسى يبكي ويدعو الله، ويقول: رب، ماذا أقول لبني إسرائيل إذا أتيتهم وقد أهلكت خيارهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p264/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p264/r1.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p264/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq recounts that after Israel’s calf worship Moses selected seventy, purified them, and brought them to Sinai; they heard God address Moses through the cloud, demanded to see God, and all died. Moses pleaded for their return so Israel would trust him; God restored them, while Moses also sought forgiveness for calf worshipers and was told they must kill themselves. The account cites Moses’ plea and repentance in 7:155–156.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p264/r1.anchor: قال: لما رجع موسى إلى قومه فرأى ما هم عليه من عبادة العجل، وقال لأخيه وللسامري ما قال، وحرق العجل وذراه في اليم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p265/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p265/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p265/r1.claim: Al-Suddi’s account says that after Israel repented from calf worship by killing some of their number, Moses chose seventy men to seek forgiveness from God for the people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p265/r1.anchor: وقال إسماعيل بن عبد الرحمن السدي الكبير: لما تابت بنو إسرائيل من عبادة العجل وتاب الله عليهم بقتل بعضهم بعضا كما أمرهم به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p265/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p265/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p265/r2.claim: The context of Ibn Ishaq’s and al-Suddi’s accounts indicates that the address to Israel concerns the seventy chosen men; most commentators report only this account.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p265/r2.anchor: وهذا السياق يقتضي أن الخطاب توجه إلى بني إسرائيل في قوله: {وإذ قلتم يا موسى لن نؤمن لك حتى نرى الله جهرة} والمراد السبعون المختارون منهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p265/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p265/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p265/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects the People of the Book’s claim that the seventy saw God: Moses himself asked and was denied, so they could not have seen Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p265/r5.anchor: وقد غلط أهل الكتاب أيضا في دعواهم أن هؤلاء رأوا الله عز وجل، فإن موسى الكليم، عليه السلام، قد سأل ذلك فمنع منه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p265/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p265/r6.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p265/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says the Israelites returned from calf worship and rejected Moses’ tablets unless God appeared and spoke to them directly; a divine anger struck and killed them, God revived them, they again rejected the book, and angels raised the mountain above them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p265/r6.anchor: قال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم في تفسير هذه الآية

JISHUMI:v1p390/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p390/r7.speaker: العامة
JISHUMI:v1p390/r7.claim: The general reading has jahra with a quiescent hāʾ.
JISHUMI:v1p390/r7.anchor: قراءة العامة جهرة بسكون الهاء، وعن ابن عباس بفتحها

JISHUMI:v1p390/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p390/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v1p390/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to read jahra with fatḥa on the hāʾ; both are language variants.
JISHUMI:v1p390/r8.anchor: وعن ابن عباس بفتحها، وهما لغتان

JISHUMI:v1p390/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p390/r9.speaker: العامة
JISHUMI:v1p390/r9.claim: The general reading is al-ṣāʿiqa with an alif.
JISHUMI:v1p390/r9.anchor: وقراءة العامة الصاعقة بالألف، وعن عمر وعثمان وعلي

JISHUMI:v1p390/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p390/r10.speaker: عمر وعثمان وعلي
JISHUMI:v1p390/r10.claim: ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, and ʿAlī are reported to read al-ṣaʿqa without the alif; both forms are language variants.
JISHUMI:v1p390/r10.anchor: وعن عمر وعثمان وعلي رضي الله عنهم: الصعقة بغير ألف، وهما لغتان

JISHUMI:v1p390/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p390/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p390/r11.claim: Īmān means assent or belief, as in the brothers’ statement in 12:17.
JISHUMI:v1p390/r11.anchor: الإيمان: التصديق، ومنه: (وما أنت بمؤمن لنا)

JISHUMI:v1p390/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p390/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p390/r12.claim: Ruʾya means perception by sight and is also used figuratively for knowledge of the heart; mirʾāt is named for seeing through it.
JISHUMI:v1p390/r12.anchor: والرؤية: الإدراك بالبصر، ثم يستعمل بمعنى العلم، ومنه رأى بقلبه

JISHUMI:v1p390/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p390/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p390/r13.claim: Jahr means openly and publicly, the opposite of secrecy; its basic sense is something appearing to direct inspection.
JISHUMI:v1p390/r13.anchor: والجهر والعلانية بمعنى يقال: جهر فلان بكلامه، وجهر بقراءته

JISHUMI:v1p390/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p390/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p390/r14.claim: A ṣāʿiqa originally is fire falling from the sky and burning what it strikes, then by extension can mean any punishment.
JISHUMI:v1p390/r14.anchor: والصاعقة: أصلها نار تنزل من السماء تحرق ما تأتي عليه

JISHUMI:v1p390/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p390/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p390/r15.claim: Naẓar is turning the eye toward something visible in search of sight with a sound faculty, and can extend to thought.
JISHUMI:v1p390/r15.anchor: والنظر: تقليب الحدقة نحو المرئي التماسا لرؤيته مع سلامة الحاسة

JISHUMI:v1p390/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p390/r16.speaker: الشاعر
JISHUMI:v1p390/r16.claim: The verb yarā is on the yafʿalu pattern because its original form is yarʾā; a poet preserves the original form.
JISHUMI:v1p390/r16.anchor: لأن أصله يرأى، قال الشاعر، وجاء به على الأصل: أري عيني ما لم ترأياه

JISHUMI:v1p390/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p390/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p390/r17.claim: Jahratan is parsed as a circumstantial accusative.

JISHUMI:v1p390/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p390/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p390/r18.claim: The address means remember when you said this; it refers to the ancestors of the Jews addressed in Muhammad’s time, whom they followed.
JISHUMI:v1p390/r18.anchor: ثم ذكر تعالى خصلة من خصال أسلافهم فقال تعالى: وإذ قلتم أي اذكروا إذ قلتم

JISHUMI:v1p390/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p390/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p390/r19.claim: One reading is that they would not believe Moses’ description of God’s attributes until they saw God directly.
JISHUMI:v1p390/r19.anchor: لا نصدقك فيما تصف الله به من الصفات حتى نراه جهرة

JISHUMI:v1p390/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p390/r20.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v1p390/r20.claim: Al-Aṣamm says they meant they would not believe Moses was a prophet until they saw God.
JISHUMI:v1p390/r20.anchor: وقيل: لا نصدقك في نبوتك، عن الأصم

JISHUMI:v1p390/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p390/r21.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p390/r21.claim: One parsing makes jahra describe the seeing, while another makes it describe their public statement.
JISHUMI:v1p390/r21.anchor: فعلى الأول الجهرة من صفة الرؤية، وعلى الثاني من صفة المقالة

JISHUMI:v1p390/r22.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p390/r22.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p390/r22.claim: The thunderbolt can mean death, as in 39:68.
JISHUMI:v1p390/r22.anchor: الصاعقة تستعمل على ثلاثة أوجه: الموت كقوله تعالى: (فصعق من في السماوات)

JISHUMI:v1p392/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p392/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p392/r1.claim: The thunderbolt can mean punishment, as in the warning about a punishment like that of ʿĀd and Thamūd.
JISHUMI:v1p392/r1.anchor: الثاني: العذاب، كقوله: (أنذرتكم صاعقة مثل صاعقة عاد وثمود)

JISHUMI:v1p392/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p392/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p392/r2.claim: It can also mean fire sent down from the sky, as in the statement that God sends thunderbolts.
JISHUMI:v1p392/r2.anchor: والثالث: نار تسقط من السماء، كقوله: (ويرسل الصواعق)

JISHUMI:v1p392/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p392/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p392/r3.claim: The people were looking at or witnessing the event.

JISHUMI:v1p392/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p392/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p392/r4.claim: They are blamed for their ancestors’ demand because they approved the action and followed their predecessors in opposing the one they had to follow.
JISHUMI:v1p392/r4.anchor: ويقال: لم قرعوا بسؤال أسلافهم الرؤية؟ قلنا: لأنهم رضوا بفعلهم وسلكوا طريقتهم

JISHUMI:v1p392/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p392/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p392/r5.claim: Another account says this condemns the Jews and consoles the Prophet, since his opponents repeat their ancestors’ opposition to Moses and impossible demands.
JISHUMI:v1p392/r5.anchor: وقيل: فيه ذم لهم وتسلية للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في أنهم بمخالفتهم إياه

JISHUMI:v1p392/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p392/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p392/r6.claim: The collective address is to Jews in Muhammad’s time, while the demand came from some ancestors; God summarizes the ancestors’ crimes.
JISHUMI:v1p392/r6.anchor: هذا خطاب لليهود الذين كانوا في زمن نبينا - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وكان هذا القول وجد من بعض أسلافهم

JISHUMI:v1p392/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p392/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p392/r7.claim: Vision can be inward or in a dream; Ibn ʿAbbās glosses jahra as publicly and Qatāda as seeing with the eyes.
JISHUMI:v1p392/r7.anchor: قد تكون كرؤية القلب، والرؤية في النوم، وقيل: علانية، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v1p392/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p392/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p392/r8.claim: Asking for vision was unbelief by consensus because it rejected the messenger; permitting vision with anthropomorphic likeness is also unbelief.
JISHUMI:v1p392/r8.anchor: هذا السؤال كفر بالإجماع؛ لأنه رد على الرسول، فأما إجازة الرؤية على جهة التشبيه فكفر

JISHUMI:v1p392/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p392/r9.speaker: أبو علي وأبو هاشم
JISHUMI:v1p392/r9.claim: Abū ʿAlī and Abū Hāshim say permitting vision without anthropomorphic likeness is not unbelief.
JISHUMI:v1p392/r9.anchor: وإجازتها من غير تشبيه قيل: ليس بكفر، عن أبي علي وأبي هاشم

JISHUMI:v1p392/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p392/r10.speaker: أبو القاسم
JISHUMI:v1p392/r10.claim: Abū al-Qāsim says permitting vision without anthropomorphic likeness is still unbelief.

JISHUMI:v1p393/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p393/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p393/r1.claim: The author ties the people’s punishment to their demand to see God and concludes that vision of God is impossible.
JISHUMI:v1p393/r1.anchor: وأنزل العقوبة بهم. وتدل على أن الرؤية لا تجوز عليه

JISHUMI:v1p393/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p393/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p393/r2.claim: God condemned the bare request for vision, without regard to any added qualification of how it would occur.
JISHUMI:v1p393/r2.anchor: أنه تعالى أنكر عليهم مجرد سؤال الرؤية، ولم يعتبر الزيادة التي أوردها

JISHUMI:v1p393/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p393/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p393/r3.claim: One explanation for the severity is that anything perceived by sight must have a quality such as body or color, so allowing vision entails likeness; another says they explicitly coupled vision with likeness by saying jahra.
JISHUMI:v1p393/r3.anchor: فجواز الرؤية يقتضي التشبيه، وقيل: لأنهم قرنوا الرؤية بالتشبيه

JISHUMI:v1p393/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p393/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p393/r4.claim: The severe punishment cut off the source of this demand for them and others.
JISHUMI:v1p393/r4.anchor: لما عظم سؤالهم عاقبهم حتى يحسم مادة السؤال منهم ومن غيرهم

JISHUMI:v1p393/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p393/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p393/r5.claim: The thunderbolt descended but did not compel them to know; otherwise restoring them and holding them accountable would be improper.
JISHUMI:v1p393/r5.anchor: وتدل الآية على أن الصاعقة نزلت، ولم يضطروا إلى المعرفة

JISHUMI:v1p393/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p393/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p393/r6.claim: After proof has been established, a community’s statement to its messenger that it will not believe is unbelief.
JISHUMI:v1p393/r6.anchor: وتدل على أن قول الأمة للرسول بعد إقامة الحجة: (لن نؤمن لك) كفر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p169#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p169#2/r1.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p169#2/r1.claim: One report says the speakers were the seventy who were struck; another says ten thousand of them made the demand.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p169#2/r1.anchor: قيل القائلون السبعون الذين صعقوا وقيل قاله عشرة آلاف منهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p169#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p169#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p169#2/r2.claim: جهرة means openly, as in reciting aloud; sight by the eye is open, while sight by the heart is quiet.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p169#2/r2.anchor: عيانا وهي مصدر من قولك جهر بالقراءة وبالدعاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p169#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p169#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p169#2/r3.claim: جهرة is accusative either as a verbal noun describing a kind of seeing or as a circumstantial phrase meaning ‘openly.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p169#2/r3.anchor: على المصدر لأنها نوع من الرؤية فنصبت بفعلها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p169#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p169#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p169#2/r4.claim: A reading with fatḥ on hāʾ makes the word either a verbal noun like غلبة or a plural of جاهر.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p169#2/r4.anchor: بفتح الهاء وهي إما مصدر كالغلبة وإما جمع جاهر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p169#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p169#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p169#2/r5.claim: Moses answered their demand by explaining that seeing God in a direction is impossible; allowing such vision makes God a body or an accident. They persisted after proof, so the thunderbolt punished their disbelief as the calf worshippers had been punished, matching the gravity of both sins.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p169#2/r5.anchor: وعرفهم أن رؤية ما لا يجوز عليه أن يكون في جهة محال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p170/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p170/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p170/r1.claim: The ṣāʿiqa is what struck and killed them; one account identifies it as fire falling from heaven and burning them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p170/r1.anchor: ما صعقهم أي أماتهم قيل نار وقعت من السماء فأحرقتهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p170/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p170/r2.speaker: قيل
