KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p170/r2.claim: Another report identifies the blow as a cry from heaven.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p170/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p170/r3.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p170/r3.claim: A further account says God sent forces whose sound they heard, and they fell dead for a day and a night.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p170/r3.anchor: وقيل أرسل الله جنودا سمعوا بحسها فخروا صعقين ميتين يوما وليلة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p170/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p170/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p170/r4.claim: Moses’s own ṣaʿq was a swoon, not death, as shown by the statement that he awoke.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p170/r4.anchor: وموسى عليه السلام لم تكن صعقته موتا ولكن غشية بدليل قوله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p170/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p170/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p170/r5.claim: Apparently, the Israelites were struck by the very thing they had asked to see.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p170/r5.anchor: والظاهر انه أصابهم ما ينظرون اليه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p170/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p170/r6.speaker: علي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p170/r6.anchor: وقرأ علي رضي الله عنه ( فأذختكم الصعقة )

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p123/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p123/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p123/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses jahratan as “openly” or in public.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p123/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p123/r2.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p123/r2.claim: Qatāda glosses it as seeing God directly, face to face.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p123/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p123/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p123/r3.claim: The root of jahr is appearance: loud recitation displays the reading, and public sin is displayed openly.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p123/r3.anchor: وأصل الجهر الظهور , ومنه الجهر بالقراءة , إنما هو إظهارها , والمجاهرة بالمعاصي : المظاهرة بها

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p123/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p123/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p123/r4.anchor: { فأخذتكم الصاعقة } يعني الموت , { وأنتم تنظرون } ما نزل بكم من الموت

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p123/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p123/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p123/r5.claim: “As you looked” means they witnessed the death that came upon them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p123/r5.anchor: { وأنتم تنظرون } ما نزل بكم من الموت

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p123/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p123/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p123/r6.claim: The people struck dead were the seventy Moses chose to hear God’s conversation with him after God accepted the repentance of the calf worshippers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p123/r6.anchor: وهم السبعون الذين اختارهم موسى ليستمعوا مناجاة ربه له بعد أن تاب على من عبد العجل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p44#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p44#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p44#3/r1.claim: جهرة means seeing openly and plainly; it is a cognate accusative or a circumstantial accusative meaning visibly.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p44#3/r1.anchor: عيانا وانتصابها على المصدر كما تنصب القرفصاء

NASAFI-FULL:v1p44#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p44#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p44#3/r2.claim: The author glosses الصاعقة as death; another account says it was fire from heaven that burned them.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p44#3/r2.anchor: أى الموت قيل هى نار جاءت من السماء فأحرقتهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p44#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p44#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p44#3/r3.claim: A report says seventy with Moses at the mountain claimed not to have worshipped the calf, demanded sight of God, then challenged Moses and were burned by lightning.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p44#3/r3.anchor: روى أن السبعين الذين كانوا مع موسى عليه السلام عند الانطلاق إلى الجبل قالوا له نحن لم نعبد العجل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p44#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p44#3/r4.speaker: المعتزلة
NASAFI-FULL:v1p44#3/r4.claim: The Muʿtazila argue that punishment for demanding to see God proves that God cannot be seen.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p44#3/r4.anchor: وتعلقت المعتزلة بهذه الآية فى نفى الرؤية

NASAFI-FULL:v1p44#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p44#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p44#3/r5.claim: The author rejects that inference: they were punished for disbelief, including saying Moses had seen God and refusing faith until they saw openly.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p44#3/r5.anchor: قلنا إنما عوقبوا بكفرهم لأن قولهم إنك رأيت الله

NASAFI-FULL:v1p44#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p44#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p44#3/r6.claim: They also withheld belief in Moses after his miracle appeared; prophets must be believed after miracles, and signs should not be demanded out of obstinacy.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p44#3/r6.anchor: ولأنهم امتنعوا عن الإيمان بموسى بعد ظهور معجزته

QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r1.claim: Idh qultum is conjoined to what precedes, ya Musa is a singular vocative, and lan nuʾmina laka means we will not believe or affirm you.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وإذ قلتم } معطوف. { ياموسى } نداء مفرد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r2.claim: The speakers are said to be the seventy Moses selected: after hearing God's speech, they made this demand; faith in prophets is obligatory after miracles, so God sent fire from heaven that burned them, then Moses prayed and they were restored as 2:56 says.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r2.anchor: قيل: هم السبعون الذين اختارهم موسى وذلك أنهم لما أسمعهم كلام الله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r3.speaker: ابن فورك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r3.claim: Ibn Furak suggests they were punished for routing the request for vision through Moses by demanding that he show them God openly, something outside his power; the wording is linked to 4:153.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r3.anchor: قال ابن فورك: يحتمل أن تكون معاقبتهم لإخراجهم طلب الرؤية عن طريقه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r4.speaker: أكثر المبتدعة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r4.claim: Most innovators deny that God can be seen in this life or the next.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r4.anchor: فأكثر المبتدعة على إنكارها في الدنيا والآخرة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r5.speaker: أهل السنة والسلف
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r5.claim: The Sunnis and early authorities hold that seeing God is possible in this life and occurs in the afterlife; on this view the request was not impossible, as Moses also asked for vision.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r5.anchor: وأهل السنة والسلف على جوازها فيهما ووقوعها فى الآخرة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r6.claim: Jahratan is a verbal noun used adverbially, meaning openly; Ibn ʿAbbas glosses it as seeing plainly, and the root denotes appearance or manifestation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r6.anchor: مصدر في موضع الحال، ومعناه علانية. وقيل عيانا قاله ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r7.claim: The same root describes audible recitation because it is made manifest, openly committing sins, and seeing an unsheltered ruler plainly.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r7.anchor: ومنه الجهر بالقراءة إنما هو إظهارها. والمجاهرة بالمعاصي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reads jahratan with fatḥa on the hāʾ; both vocalizations are dialectal variants, like zahra and zuhrah.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r9.claim: One analysis makes jahratan describe the Israelites' speech to Moses, requiring fronting and delaying: wa-idh qultum jahratan ya Musa.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r9.anchor: أحدهما: أنه صفة لخطابهم لموسى أنهم جهروا به وأعلنوا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r10.claim: Alternatively, jahratan describes the requested sight of God openly, leaving the wording in its usual order and distinguishing waking sight from vision in a dream.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r10.anchor: الثاني: أنه صفة لما سألوه من رؤية الله تعالى أن يروه جهرة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r11.speaker: عمر وعثمان وعلي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r11.claim: Umar, Uthman, and Ali read al-saʿqa in place of al-saʿiqa; Ibn Muhaysin uses this reading throughout the Qur'an.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r12.claim: Wa-antum tanẓurun is a circumstantial clause.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r12.anchor: { وأنتم تنظرون } جملة في موضع الحال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r13.claim: To explain how they died while looking, one says Arabic describes houses of a clan as facing one another; thus they could be in view of each other.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r13.anchor: فالجواب أن العرب تقول: دور آل فلان تراءى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56/r14.claim: Another explanation is that they watched their own condition, the death that came upon them, and the traces of the lightning strike.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56#2/r5.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56#2/r5.claim: One view, preferred by al-Qurtubi, holds that those restored after death remain morally obligated, lest no rational person be subject to worship duties.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56#2/r5.anchor: قال الماوردي: واختلف في بقاء تكليف من أعيد بعد موته ومعاينة الأحوال المضطرة إلى المعرفة على قولين: أحدهما: بقاء تكليفهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56#2/r6.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56#2/r6.claim: The other view says their obligation ends because accountability rests on inferential proof, not knowledge made necessary by directly witnessing extraordinary events.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56#2/r6.anchor: قال الماوردي: واختلف في بقاء تكليف من أعيد بعد موته ومعاينة الأحوال المضطرة إلى المعرفة على قولين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56#2/r7.claim: Al-Qurtubi says obligation remained: Israelites saw the falling mountain and encircling fire, yet remained accountable; the people of Jonah were likewise obligated.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:55-56#2/r7.anchor: قلت: والأول أصح، فإن بني إسرائيل قد رأوا الجبل في الهواء ساقطا عليهم والنار محيطة بهم وذلك مما اضطرهم إلى الإيمان

QASHANI:2:55-57/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:55-57/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:55-57/r1.claim: Their refusal means they would not attain true faith through Moses' guidance until reaching direct witnessing and vision.
QASHANI:2:55-57/r1.anchor: لأجل هدايتك الإيمان الحقيقي حتى تصل إلى مقام المشاهدة والعيان

QASHANI:2:55-57/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:55-57/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:55-57/r2.claim: The thunderbolt is death as annihilation in the self-disclosure of the Essence; they were observing or witnessing it.
QASHANI:2:55-57/r2.anchor: صاعقة الموت الذي هو الفناء في التجلي الذاتي

RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r1.claim: The sixth favor recalls the demand, the thunderbolt, and revival: God brought them back so they could repent, escape punishment, and gain reward.
RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r1.anchor: اذكروا نعمتي حين قلتم لموسى لن نؤمن لك حتى نرى الله جهرة فأخذتكم الصاعقة ثم أحييتكم

RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r2.claim: The story warns Muhammad’s contemporaries against actions that could bring the same punishment upon them.
RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r2.anchor: وثانيها : أن فيها تحذيرا لمن كان في زمان نبينا محمد

RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r3.claim: The Israelites’ denial of Moses despite witnessing great signs parallels their descendants’ denial of Muhammad; God withholds comparable signs because their rejection would merit punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r3.anchor: وثالثها : تشبيههم في جحودهم معجزات النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بأسلافهم في جحود نبوة موسى

RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r4.claim: The account consoles Muhammad and steadies him to endure rejection as the resolute messengers endured it.
RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r4.anchor: ورابعها : فيه تسلية للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مما كان يلاقي منهم وتثبيت لقلبه على الصبر

RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r5.claim: The ancestors’ repeated rejection of Moses despite clear signs answers the claim that scriptural People of the Book should readily accept Muhammad because they knew of him.
RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r5.anchor: أسلافهم مع مشاهدتهم تلك الآيات الباهرة على نبوة موسى عليه السلام كانوا يرتدون كل وقت ويتحكمون عليه

RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r6.claim: Muhammad’s accurate telling of these accounts, although he was unlettered and never studied, proves that they came by revelation.
RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r6.anchor: وسادسها : لما أخبر محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام عن هذه القصص مع أنه كان أميا لم يشتغل بالتعلم

RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r7.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r7.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Moses returned, destroyed the calf, and took seventy chosen men to hear God. A cloud hid Moses; they heard divine commands, then demanded direct sight, died by the thunderbolt, and were revived after Moses prayed.
RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r7.anchor: قال محمد بن اسحاق : لما رجع موسى عليه السلام من الطور إلى قومه

RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r8.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r8.claim: In Ibn Ishaq’s account, after the revival Moses asks for Israel’s repentance from calf worship; God requires them to kill themselves as repentance.
RAZI-FULL:v3p78/r8.anchor: حتى رد الله إليهم أرواحهم وطلب توبة بني إسرائيل من عبادة العجل فقال : لا إلا أن يقتلوا أنفسهم

RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r1.speaker: السدي
RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r1.claim: Al-Suddi places the event after repentance through mutual killing: seventy survivors ask to see God, die, and are revived; learning they had worshipped the calf, they ask Moses to make them prophets and God grants his prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r1.anchor: قال السدي : لما تاب بنو إسرائيل من عبادة العجل بأن قتلوا أنفسهم

RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r2.claim: The verse does not decide which of the two reported chronologies is correct, or whether the sight-seekers were calf-worshippers or other Israelites.
RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r2.anchor: ليس في الآية ما يدل على ترجيح أحد القولين على الآخر وكذلك ليس فيها ما يدل على أن الذين سألوا الرؤية

RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r3.claim: They say they will not believe or acknowledge Moses’ prophethood until they see God openly, meaning with their eyes.
RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r3.anchor: فمعناه لا نصدقك ولا نعترف بنبوتك حتى نرى الله جهرة ( أي ) عيانا

RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r4.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r4.claim: Al-Kashshaf analyzes jahratan as a verbal noun from speaking aloud, a kind of seeing treated as a cognate accusative, or a circumstantial accusative meaning openly.
RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r4.anchor: جهرت بالقراءة وبالدعاء كأن الذي يرى بالعين جاهر بالرؤية

RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r5.claim: A reading with fatḥa on the hāʾ is reported; jahratan can be a verbal noun like ghalabatan or a plural meaning those who make it manifest.
RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r5.anchor: وقرىء جهرة بفتح الهاء وهي إما مصدر كالغلبة وإما جمع جاهر

RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r6.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r6.claim: Al-Qaffal derives jahr from manifest appearance, citing uncovering an object, clearing mud from a well until its water appears, a loud voice, and a bright-looking face.
RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r6.anchor: وقال القفال أصل الجهرة من الظهور يقال جهرت الشيء ( إذا ) كشفته

RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r7.claim: Their use of jahratan stresses that they demand visible sight, not knowledge or an imagined vision like one in sleep.
RAZI-FULL:v3p79/r7.anchor: وإنما قالوا : جهرة تأكيدا لئلا يتوهم متوهم أن المراد بالرؤية العلم أو التخيل

RAZI-FULL:v3p79#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p79#2/r1.speaker: القاضي عبد الجبار
RAZI-FULL:v3p79#2/r1.claim: Qadi ʿAbd al-Jabbar argues that if seeing God were possible, asking for it would be permissible and should not have brought punishment, just as asking for different food did not.
RAZI-FULL:v3p79#2/r1.anchor: قال القاضي عبد الجبار : إنها لو كانت جائزة لكانوا قد التمسوا أمرا مجوزا

RAZI-FULL:v3p79#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p79#2/r2.speaker: أبو الحسين
RAZI-FULL:v3p79#2/r2.claim: Abu al-Husayn argues that God presents the demand as grave; if vision were permissible, it would be like asking for a dead person to be raised as a sign, not a cause for the thunderbolt.
RAZI-FULL:v3p79#2/r2.anchor: وقال أبو الحسين في كتاب التصفح : إن الله تعالى ما ذكر سؤال الرؤية إلا استعظمه

RAZI-FULL:v3p79#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p79#2/r3.speaker: أبو الحسين
RAZI-FULL:v3p79#2/r3.claim: Abu al-Husayn cites 4:153: the People of the Book asked for a heavenly book and then demanded sight, which God calls wrongdoing and punishes; if vision were permissible, it would be an extra miracle request.
RAZI-FULL:v3p79#2/r3.anchor: وقال أبو الحسين في كتاب التصفح : إن الله تعالى ما ذكر سؤال الرؤية إلا استعظمه

RAZI-FULL:v3p79#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p79#2/r4.speaker: أبو الحسين
RAZI-FULL:v3p79#2/r4.claim: He answers that although a heavenly book is possible, the apparent wording treats both the book and seeing God as forbidden; the book’s case is set aside, leaving the sight request condemned.
RAZI-FULL:v3p79#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو الحسين في كتاب التصفح : إن الله تعالى ما ذكر سؤال الرؤية إلا استعظمه

RAZI-FULL:v3p79#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p79#2/r5.speaker: أبو الحسين
RAZI-FULL:v3p79#2/r5.claim: Abu al-Husayn also cites 25:21, where those who do not expect the meeting ask to see their Lord and are called greatly arrogant; a permissible vision request would be like asking for a dead person’s revival.
RAZI-FULL:v3p79#2/r5.anchor: وقال أبو الحسين في كتاب التصفح : إن الله تعالى ما ذكر سؤال الرؤية إلا استعظمه

RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r1.claim: Al-Razi says the Muʿtazilite arguments all assume that a request for any possible thing cannot be disobedient, which does not follow from examples about food or other signs.
RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r1.anchor: وهو أن الرؤية لو كانت جائزة لما كان سؤالها عتوا ومنكرا / وذلك ممنوع

RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r2.claim: In 4:153 and 25:21 the request for vision is paired with an agreed-possible request for a book or angels, so the combined condemnation does not prove vision itself impossible.
RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r2.anchor: ما ذكر الرؤية إلا وذكر معها شيئا ممكنا حكمنا بجوازه بالاتفاق وهو إما نزول الكتاب من السماء أو نزول الملائكة

RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r3.claim: Al-Razi rejects the claim that condemnation must mean the requested thing is impossible: the Muʿtazilites provide no proof beyond examples, which cannot establish that rule.
RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r3.anchor: إنك ما أقمت دليلا على أن الاستعظام لا يتحقق إلا إذا كان المطلوب ممتنعا وإنما عولت فيه على ضروب الأمثلة

RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r4.claim: One possible reason the request was condemned is that vision of God is available only in the afterlife, making a demand for it in this world improper.
RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r4.anchor: أحدها : أن رؤية الله تعالى لا تحصل إلا في الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r5.claim: Another possibility is that seeing God entails the end of religious obligation; on the Muʿtazilite account it brings necessary knowledge, which itself precludes obligation.
RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r5.anchor: أن حكم الله تعالى أن يزيل التكليف عن العبد حال ما يرى الله فكان طلب الرؤية طلبا لإزالة التكليف

RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r6.claim: A third possibility is that once proofs of the claimant are complete, demanding extra proofs is obstinacy deserving rebuke.
RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r6.anchor: لما تمت الدلائل على صدق المدعي كان طلب الدلائل الزائدة تعنتا والمتعنت يستوجب التعنيف

RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r7.claim: A fourth possibility is that God knows an important benefit in preventing sight in this world, just as he knows harm in sending down books or angels from heaven.
RAZI-FULL:v3p80/r7.anchor: لا يمتنع أن يعلم الله تعالى أن في منع الخلق عن رؤيته سبحانه في الدنيا ضربا من المصلحة المهمة

RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r1.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say al-ṣāʿiqah means death, citing the verse that all in heaven and earth will be struck down.
RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r1.anchor: الأول : أنها هي الموت وهو قول الحسن وقتادة

RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r2.claim: Al-Razi rejects the death interpretation because the Israelites could not be looking at death itself when it struck them.
RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى : { فأخذتكم الصاعقة وأنتم تنظرون } ولو كانت الصاعقة هي الموت

RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r3.claim: Moses was also described as ṣaʿiq, yet recovered; recovery is from fainting, not death.
RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r3.anchor: الإفاقة لا تكون عن الموت بل عن الغشي

RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r4.claim: The word ṣāʿiqah denotes what strikes or stuns, pointing to the cause of death rather than death itself.
RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r4.anchor: أن الصاعقة وهي التي تصعق وذلك إشارة إلى سبب الموت

RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r5.claim: The fact that the blow came while they watched makes the punishment more severe than if it had struck unexpectedly; the phrase emphasizes its gravity.
RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r5.anchor: ورابعها : أن ورودها وهم مشاهدون لها أعظم في باب العقوبة منها

RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r6.speaker: المحققون
RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r6.claim: The investigators say al-ṣāʿiqah is the cause of death, supported by the account in al-Aʿraf that calls the event a quake.
RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r6.anchor: القول الثاني : وهو قول المحققين : إن الصاعقة هي سبب الموت

RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r7.claim: Three proposed causes are a fire from heaven, a cry from heaven, or God-sent hosts whose faint sound made them fall dead for a day and a night.
RAZI-FULL:v3p80#2/r7.anchor: واختلفوا في أن ذلك السبب أي شيء كان على ثلاثة أوجه

STUDYQURAN:2:55/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r1.claim: The thunderbolt is etymologically related to Moses’ swoon and the swoon of heaven and earth at the trumpet blast on Judgment Day.
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r1.anchor: The thunderbolt, related etymologically to Moses’ swoon (7:143) and the “swoon” of the heavens and earth at the blowing of the trumpet

STUDYQURAN:2:55/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r2.claim: Thunderbolts also punish ʿĀd and Thamūd; the Thamūd were seized by one as they looked on.
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r2.anchor: is also a punishment for the ʿĀd and the Thamūd (41:13). The Thamūd’s thunderbolt also seized them as they looked on.

STUDYQURAN:2:55/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r3.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r3.claim: Ṣāʿiqah can also mean a great calamity or destruction, a great cry or noise, fire, or an earthquake.
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r3.anchor: It can also refer more generally to a great calamity or destruction, or a great cry or noise, a fire, or an earthquake (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:2:55/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r4.speaker: IK, R
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r4.claim: Some commentators identify this with 7:155: after the calf’s destruction, Moses took seventy chosen Israelites who had worshipped it; their request to see God was followed by a fatal thunderbolt, then Moses prayed and God revived them.
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r4.anchor: Some commentators (IK, R) identify this verse with the incident described in 7:155, which would mean that after the destruction of the calf, Moses went up the mountain with seventy of the choicest Israelites

STUDYQURAN:2:55/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r5.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r5.claim: Other commentators regard 2:55 and 7:155 as separate incidents.
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r5.anchor: Others (JJ) consider 2:55 and 7:155 as separate incidents

STUDYQURAN:2:55/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r6.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r6.claim: Some commentators take no firm position on whether 2:55 and 7:155 describe the same event.
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r6.anchor: some take no firm position (R). The word rendered thunderbolt

STUDYQURAN:2:55/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r7.claim: Ṣāʿiqah has a broader range than rajfah, used for the calamity in 7:155, though the two could denote the same event.

STUDYQURAN:2:55/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r8.claim: Jahratan means seeing with one’s eyes or publicly; the word can also describe speech.
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r8.anchor: means to see with one’s eyes, or simply “publicly.”

STUDYQURAN:2:55/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r9.claim: The demand to see God is also cross-referenced with 4:153.
STUDYQURAN:2:55/r9.anchor: Cf. 4:153. The thunderbolt, related etymologically to Moses’ swoon

TAB-FULL:v1p688/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p688/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p688/r1.claim: Their demand meant that they would not believe Moses until they saw God plainly with their own eyes, with the veil lifted.
TAB-FULL:v1p688/r1.anchor: حتى ننظر إليه بأبصارنا، كما تجهر الركية

TAB-FULL:v1p688/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p688/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p688/r2.claim: Al-Tabari derives jahra from clearing mud that covers a well until its water appears clear; the word then means making something manifest to sight.
TAB-FULL:v1p688/r2.anchor: قد جهرت الركية أجهرها جهرا وجهرة؛ ولذلك قيل: قد جهر فلان بهذا الأمر مجاهرة وجهارا

TAB-FULL:v1p688/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p688/r3.speaker: الفرزدق بن غالب
TAB-FULL:v1p688/r3.claim: Al-Farazdaq's use of jahāran witnesses to the sense of doing something openly and visibly.
TAB-FULL:v1p688/r3.anchor: من اللائي يضل الألف منه … مسحا من مخالفته جهارا

TAB-FULL:v1p688/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p688/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p688/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses jahra as publicly, or openly.
TAB-FULL:v1p688/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: قال ابن عباس: " {حتى نرى الله جهرة}

TAB-FULL:v1p688/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p688/r5.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v1p688/r5.claim: Al-Rabi glosses the demand as seeing God directly.
TAB-FULL:v1p688/r5.anchor: عن الربيع: " {حتى نرى الله جهرة} [البقرة: 55] يقول: عيانا

TAB-FULL:v1p688/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p688/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v1p688/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets the demand as asking God to appear to them.
TAB-FULL:v1p688/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد: " {حتى نرى الله جهرة} [البقرة: 55] حتى يطلع إلينا

TAB-FULL:v1p688/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p688/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p688/r7.claim: Qatada glosses the demand as seeing God directly.
TAB-FULL:v1p688/r7.anchor: عن قتادة: " {حتى نرى الله جهرة} [البقرة: 55] أي عيانا

TAB-FULL:v1p688/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p688/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p688/r8.claim: Al-Tabari recalls Israel's other rebellions and warns the Jews around the Prophet to follow their ancestors in rejecting Muhammad despite knowing his truth.
TAB-FULL:v1p688/r8.anchor: ومرة يعبدون العجل من دون الله، ومرة يقولون لا نصدقك حتى نرى الله جهرة

TAB-FULL:v1p690/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p690/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p690/r1.claim: Qatada says the thunderbolt killed them.
TAB-FULL:v1p690/r1.anchor: عن قتادة: " في قوله: {فأخذتهم الصاعقة} [البقرة: 55] قال: ماتوا

TAB-FULL:v1p690/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p690/r2.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v1p690/r2.claim: Al-Rabi says they heard a sound, were struck down by it, and died.
TAB-FULL:v1p690/r2.anchor: عن الربيع: " {فأخذتكم الصاعقة} [البقرة: 55] قال: سمعوا صوتا، فصعقوا. يقول: فماتوا

TAB-FULL:v1p690/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p690/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v1p690/r3.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the thunderbolt as fire.

TAB-FULL:v1p690/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p690/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v1p690/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq says a tremor, which is the thunderbolt, struck them all dead.
TAB-FULL:v1p690/r4.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: «أخذتهم الرجفة وهي الصاعقة فماتوا جميعا»

TAB-FULL:v1p690/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p690/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p690/r5.claim: Al-Tabari defines ṣāʿiqa broadly as any overwhelming, terrifying event causing death, bodily harm, loss of reason or understanding, or loss of a faculty, whether sound, fire, earthquake, or tremor.
TAB-FULL:v1p690/r5.anchor: وأصل الصاعقة: كل أمر هائل رآه أو عاينه أو أصابه حتى يصير من هوله وعظيم شأنه إلى هلاك وعطب

TAB-FULL:v1p690/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p690/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p690/r6.claim: The term can describe someone struck unconscious but still alive: Moses fell ṣaʿiqan and later awoke, so the word does not necessarily mean death.
TAB-FULL:v1p690/r6.anchor: ومما يدل على أنه قد يكون مصعوقا وهو حي غير ميت، قول الله عز وجل: {وخر موسى صعقا} [الأعراف: 143]

TAB-FULL:v1p690/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p690/r7.speaker: جرير بن عطية
TAB-FULL:v1p690/r7.claim: Jarir's comparison of the living Farazdaq to a monkey struck by lightning supports the nonfatal sense of being stunned.
TAB-FULL:v1p690/r7.anchor: ومنه قول جرير بن عطية: وهل كان الفرزدق غير قرد … أصابته الصواعق فاستدارا

TAB-FULL:v1p692/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p692/r4.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v1p692/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Moses selected seventy after the calf episode to seek pardon; after hearing God speak, they demanded to see Him, died by the thunderbolt, and were restored after Moses pleaded, while repentance still required self-killing.
TAB-FULL:v1p692/r4.anchor: عن محمد بن إسحاق، قال: " لما رجع موسى إلى قومه، ورأى ما هم فيه من عبادة العجل

TAB-FULL:v1p696/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p696/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v1p696/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says Moses brought seventy after Israel repented for the calf by mutual killing; they demanded to see God, died and were revived, then asked to be prophets, and God made them prophets, with the sequence advanced and delayed.
TAB-FULL:v1p696/r1.anchor: عن السدي: " لما تابت بنو إسرائيل من عبادة العجل، وتاب الله عليهم بقتل بعضهم بعضا كما أمرهم به

TAB-FULL:v1p696/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p696/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v1p696/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says that after the calf repentance, they demanded God's appearance to authenticate the Torah, were struck dead despite their repentance, then revived, rejected the tablets, and God raised a mountain above them.
TAB-FULL:v1p696/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد: " قال لهم موسى لما رجع من عند ربه بالألواح، قد كتب فيها التوراة

TAB-FULL:v1p697/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p697/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p697/r1.claim: Qatada says God raised them after the thunderbolt so they could complete their remaining lifespans.

TAB-FULL:v1p697/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p697/r2.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
TAB-FULL:v1p697/r2.claim: Al-Rabi says the seventy chosen by Moses heard God's speech, demanded to see Him, heard a sound and died; they were restored to complete their lifespans because their death was punitive.
TAB-FULL:v1p697/r2.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس: " في قوله: {فأخذتهم الصاعقة} [البقرة: 55] قال: هم السبعون الذين اختارهم موسى فساروا معه

TAB-FULL:v1p697/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p697/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p697/r3.claim: Al-Tabari says no report about why they made the demand is established by proof; some accounts may be true, but the audience need only know the Qur'an's account, which reproaches those denying Muhammad despite clear proof.
TAB-FULL:v1p697/r3.anchor: ولا خبر عندنا بصحة شيء مما قاله من ذكرنا قوله في سبب قيلهم ذلك لموسى تقوم به حجة فتسلم لهم

SULAMI:v1p60#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p60#2/r1.speaker: بعض البغداديين
SULAMI:v1p60#2/r1.claim: Whoever gazes at the Divine Essence with reverence is clothed in attributes of might and majesty, then seeks refuge in the language of helplessness and repentance.
SULAMI:v1p60#2/r1.anchor: قال بعض البغداديين : من طالع الذات بعين الحرمة الحق ، ومن طالعها بالحرمة أولى عليه صفات الجبروت والعظمة

TUSTARI:2:55/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:55/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:55/r1.claim: Al-ṣāʿiqa means death, and more broadly any destructive punishment God sends upon whichever servants He wills.
TUSTARI:2:55/r1.anchor: الصاعقة: الموت، والصاعقة: كل عذاب مهلك ينزله الله تعالى

TUSTARI:2:55/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:55/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:55/r2.claim: The punished witnessed it directly, while God showed it to others as a lesson and warning.
TUSTARI:2:55/r2.anchor: فينظرون إلى ذلك عيانا، ويريه غيرهم فيهم اعتبارا وتحذيرا

TABRISI:2:55/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:55/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:55/r1.claim: The phrase means they would not believe or accept Moses as truthful.
TABRISI:2:55/r1.anchor: لن نؤمن لك أي لن نصدقك يقال آمن به وآمن له

TABRISI:2:55/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:55/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:55/r2.claim: Seeing first means visual perception, then by extension knowledge; the verb also has distinct sight, opinion, and dream usages.
TABRISI:2:55/r2.anchor: والرؤية الإدراك بالبصر ثم يستعمل بمعنى العلم يقال رأى ببصره رؤية ورأى من الرأي رأيا

TABRISI:2:55/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:55/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:55/r3.claim: Raʾy can mean fine appearance and bearing; Jarir’s verse supplies an Arabic usage witness for raʾy.
TABRISI:2:55/r3.anchor: والرأي حسن الشارة والهيئة قال جرير:

TABRISI:2:55/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:55/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:55/r4.claim: Jahr denotes appearance and open disclosure; the author distinguishes it from direct perception by relating them to the perceived object and perceiver.
TABRISI:2:55/r4.anchor: والجهر والعلامة والمعاينة نظائر يقال جهر بكلامه وبقراءته جهرا إذا علن

TABRISI:2:55/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:55/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:55/r5.claim: Seeing may occur in sleep or by the heart, but jahra makes the seeing literal eyesight rather than imagination.
TABRISI:2:55/r5.anchor: وقد تكون الرؤية في المنام والرؤية بالقلب فإذا قال جهرة لم يكن إلا رؤية العين على التحقيق دون التخييل

TABRISI:2:55/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:55/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:55/r6.claim: Ṣāʿiqa has three senses: fire from heaven, death, or punishment, illustrated respectively by other Qurʾanic passages.

TABRISI:2:55/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:55/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:55/r7.claim: Ḥattā means until, governs a noun, and makes narā subjunctive through an implicit an; the phrase is construed in the genitive and as the object of believe.
TABRISI:2:55/r7.anchor: حتى بمعنى إلى وهي الجارة للاسم

TABRISI:2:55/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:55/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:55/r8.claim: The strongest interpretation is that they would not accept Moses’ claim to be a commissioned prophet until God appeared openly and confirmed it.

TABRISI:2:55/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:55/r9.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:55/r9.claim: Another interpretation has them rejecting Moses’ account of God’s attributes and what may or may not be ascribed to Him until they see God.
TABRISI:2:55/r9.anchor: وقيل معناه إنا لا نصدقك فيما تخبر به من صفات الله تعالى وما يجوز عليه وما لا يجوز عليه

TABRISI:2:55/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:55/r10.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:55/r10.claim: A further view says they demanded to see God before believing that the Torah on the tablets came from God.
TABRISI:2:55/r10.anchor: وقيل إنه لما جاءهم بالألواح وفيها التوراة قالوا لن نؤمن بأن هذا من عند الله

TABRISI:2:55/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:55/r11.speaker: بعضهم
TABRISI:2:55/r11.claim: Some take jahra as modifying their public, outspoken address to Moses, rather than their seeing; the author prefers the first interpretation.
TABRISI:2:55/r11.anchor: وقال بعضهم إن قوله جهرة صفة لخطابهم لموسى أنهم جهروا به وأعلنوه

TABRISI:2:55#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:55#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:55#2/r1.claim: Here ṣāʿiqa means death, and they watched the signs leading to death.
TABRISI:2:55#2/r1.anchor: إلى أسباب الموت وقيل إلى النار

TABRISI:2:55#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:55#2/r2.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:55#2/r2.claim: Another view says they were watching the fire.
TABRISI:2:55#2/r2.anchor: وقيل إلى النار وإنما قرع الله سبحانه اليهود بسؤال أسلافهم الرؤية

TABRISI:2:55#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:55#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:55#2/r3.claim: The Jews are rebuked for repeating their forebears’ resistance to the prophet they had to follow, including demands for another god, worship of the calf, and a demand to see God.
TABRISI:2:55#2/r3.anchor: وإنما قرع الله سبحانه اليهود بسؤال أسلافهم الرؤية من حيث إنهم سلكوا طريقتهم في المخالفة

TABRISI:2:55#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:55#2/r4.speaker: أبو القاسم البلخي
TABRISI:2:55#2/r4.claim: Al-Balkhi argues the verse rejects both their defiance of Moses and their allowance of vision of God, and cites 4:153 as corroboration.
TABRISI:2:55#2/r4.anchor: واستدل أبو القاسم البلخي بهذه الآية على أن الرؤية لا تجوز على الله تعالى قال لأنها إنكار

TABRISI:2:55#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:55#2/r5.speaker: أبو القاسم البلخي
TABRISI:2:55#2/r5.claim: He connects this demand with 4:153, where they asked Moses to show them God openly, as evidence that both parts of the demand are rejected.
TABRISI:2:55#2/r5.anchor: ويؤيد ذلك قوله تعالى فقد سألوا موسى أكبر من ذلك فقالوا أرنا الله جهرة

TABRISI:2:55#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:55#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:55#2/r6.claim: The author says Moses’ request to see God was made on behalf of his people; the Torah’s adherents agree he asked for vision only once, on their behalf.
TABRISI:2:55#2/r6.anchor: لأنه لا خلاف بين أهل التوراة أن موسى ع يسأل الرؤية إلا دفعة واحدة وهي التي سألها لقومه

THALABI:v1p198#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p198#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p198#2/r1.claim: As the occasion, God ordered Moses to bring selected Israelites to seek pardon for worshipping the calf; seventy men fasted and purified themselves before going to Sinai.
THALABI:v1p198#2/r1.anchor: وذلك أن الله أمر موسى أن يأتيه في ناس من بني إسرائيل يعتذرون إليه من عبادة العجل، فاختار سبعين رجلا

THALABI:v1p198#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p198#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p198#2/r2.claim: The group asked Moses to let them hear God; in the cloud on the mountain they prostrated and heard God address Moses and command them to worship Him alone.
THALABI:v1p198#2/r2.anchor: قالوا: اطلب لنا نسمع كلام ربنا، فقال: أفعل، فلما دنا موسى من الجبل وقع عليه عمود الغمام

THALABI:v1p198#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p198#2/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p198#2/r3.claim: After the cloud lifted, they demanded to see God openly, and a fire from heaven burned them all in the account’s main version.
THALABI:v1p198#2/r3.anchor: فلما فرغ موسى وانكشف الغمام أقبل إليهم، فقالوا له: لن نؤمن لك حتى نرى الله جهرة

THALABI:v1p198#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p198#2/r4.speaker: وهب
THALABI:v1p198#2/r4.claim: Wahb says God sent a heavenly force; when the Israelites heard its sound, they died for a day and a night.
THALABI:v1p198#2/r4.anchor: وقال وهب: أرسل الله عز وجل عليهم جندا من السماء فلما سمعوا بحسها ماتوا يوما وليلة

THALABI:v1p198#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p198#2/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p198#2/r5.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī glosses al-ṣāʿiqa as the destroyer.
THALABI:v1p198#2/r5.anchor: والصاعقة: المهلكة، فذلك قوله: وإذ قلتم

THALABI:v1p198#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p198#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p198#2/r6.claim: The phrase means they would not believe or affirm Moses until they saw God openly.
THALABI:v1p198#2/r6.anchor: فذلك قوله: وإذ قلتم يا موسى لن نؤمن لن نصدقك حتى نرى الله جهرة

THALABI:v1p198#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p198#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v1p198#2/r7.claim: The general reading has a quiescent hāʾ in jahra; Ibn ʿAbbās reads it with fatḥa, and both forms are dialectal variants.
THALABI:v1p198#2/r7.anchor: قرأه العامة بجزم الهاء، وقرأ ابن عباس: (جهرة) بفتح الهاء وهما لغتان مثل زهره

THALABI:v1p199/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p199/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p199/r1.claim: Jahra means direct sight with no veil between them and God; the root sense of jahr is uncovering, supported by poetry.
THALABI:v1p199/r1.anchor: جهرة أي معاينة بلا ساتر بيننا وبينه، وأصل الجهر من الكشف.

THALABI:v1p199/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p199/r2.speaker: عمر وعثمان وعلي
THALABI:v1p199/r2.claim: ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, and ʿAlī read al-ṣaʿqa without the alif; the remaining readers have al-ṣāʿiqa with alif, and both are linguistic forms.
THALABI:v1p199/r2.anchor: قرأ عمر وعثمان وعلي (رضي الله عنهم) : (الصعقة) بغير ألف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p538#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p538#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p538#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses jahra as seeing God openly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p538#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: حتى نراه علانية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p538#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p538#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p538#2/r2.claim: Qatada glosses it as seeing God directly, while the author distinguishes direct ocular vision from dream or heart vision.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p538#2/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: عيانا (¬6). وقد تكون الرؤية غير جهرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p538#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p538#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p538#2/r3.claim: Vision can be indirect, as in a dream or by the heart; specifying jahra makes this actual ocular vision, not an imagined vision.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p538#2/r3.anchor: وقد تكون الرؤية غير جهرة كالرؤية في النوم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p538#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p538#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p538#2/r4.claim: Linguists define jahra as uncovered and manifest; the root means revealing, as when one clears mud from a well to expose its water, and Abu Zayd uses it for declaring speech aloud.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p538#2/r4.anchor: قال أهل اللغة: معنى قوله: جهرة أي غير مستتر عنا بشيء، وأصل الجهر في اللغة: الكشف والإظهار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p538#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p538#2/r5.speaker: الأعشى
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p538#2/r5.claim: Al-Aʿsha’s poem illustrates jahāra as the display of beauty and exposure through whiteness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p538#2/r5.anchor: قال الأعشى: وسبتك حين تبسمت ... بين الأريكة والستاره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p538#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p538#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p538#2/r6.claim: Jahra in the verse is a faʿla form from jahr, a verbal noun used to denote the object.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p538#2/r6.anchor: فالجهرة في هذه الآية: فعلة من الجهر، وهو مصدر يراد به المفعول

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r1.claim: Al-ṣāʿiqa is what strikes them, namely death, as the next verse says they were raised after dying.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r1.anchor: يعني ما تصعقون منه، أي: تموتون، لأنه قال:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: الصاعقة: الموت (¬2)، ومضى الكلام في الصاعقة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r3.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r3.claim: Exegetes say God sent Moses with seventy Israelite notables to repent from calf worship; after hearing God, they demanded direct sight when the cloud lifted, and a heavenly fire consumed them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r3.anchor: قال المفسرون: إن الله تعالى أمر موسى أن يأتيه في ناس من بني إسرائيل يعتذرون إليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says they watched one another as the thunderbolt descended.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r4.anchor: يريد نظر بعضهم إلى بعض عند نزول الصاعقة (¬5)، قاله (¬6) ابن زيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r5.claim: They were punished for refusing faith in Moses after his miracle until they could see God; believing a messenger after a manifest miracle is obligatory, and demanding further signs is impermissible.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r5.anchor: لأنهم امتنعوا من الإيمان بموسى بعد ظهور معجزته حتى يريهم ربهم جهرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r6.claim: Moses asked from faith, confirmation, and longing, whereas these people asked doubtingly, denying, and obstinately, so only they were punished.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r6.anchor: ولما كان سؤال موسى إيمانا منه وتصديقا واشتياقا لم يعاقب عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r7.speaker: بعضهم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r7.claim: Some say Moses’ companions believed seeing God impossible and used it to mean they would never believe, like the impossible condition in 7:40; hence their punishment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم: إن أصحاب موسى اعتقدوا إحالة الرؤية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r8.claim: The verse rebukes them for opposing a messenger despite his miracle, as their forebears opposed Moses, and warns the present audience against the same fate.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p540/r8.anchor: تتضمن التوبيخ لهم على مخالفة الرسول عليه السلام مع قيام معجزته

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p49#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p49#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p49#2/r1.claim: Jahratan means openly and visibly, not in sleep or any other state.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p49#2/r1.anchor: أي علانية ظاهرا، لا في نوم ولا في غيره.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p49#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p49#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p49#2/r2.claim: The thunderbolt here means death, as the next verse says they were raised after their death.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p49#2/r2.anchor: أي الموت. يدلك على ذلك قوله: {ثم بعثناكم من بعد موتكم}

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r1.claim: The speakers were the men Moses selected to apologize to God for the calf worship; they spoke after hearing God and after Moses finished his communion.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r1.anchor: الذين اختارهم موسى عليه السلام ليعتذروا إلى الله سبحانه من عبادة العجل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r2.claim: They told Moses they would not believe or affirm what he said.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r2.anchor: لن نصدقك { حتى نرى الله جهرة }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r3.claim: They demanded to see God visibly, with nothing veiling Him from them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r3.anchor: أي: عيانا لا يستره عنا شيء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r4.claim: The ṣāʿiqa was a fire sent down from heaven that burned them all.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r4.anchor: وهي نار جاءت من السماء فأحرقتهم جميعا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r5.claim: They were looking at the ṣāʿiqa as it descended.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r5.anchor: إليها حين نزلت، وإنما أخذتهم الصاعقة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r6.claim: They were punished for refusing faith in Moses after his miracle appeared and demanding that God be shown openly; faith in prophets is obligatory after a miracle, and demanding further miracles is impermissible.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r6.anchor: والإيمان بالأنبياء واجب بعد ظهور معجزتهم، ولا يجوز اقتراح المعجزات عليه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r7.claim: The verse rebukes their disobedience to the Messenger despite his established miracle, as their ancestors disobeyed Moses despite manifest signs.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:55/r7.anchor: وهذه الآية توبيخ لهم على مخالفة الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

ELMALILI:2:55-56/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r1.claim: The Israelites demanded a direct sight of God before believing Moses; the calamity struck them into a near-death state in which they could only stare, not move.
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r1.anchor: kımıldanmaya dermanınız kalmamış, sade bakıp duruyordunuz

ELMALILI:2:55-56/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r2.speaker: Birçokları
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r2.claim: Many understood the phrase to mean they were struck dead while looking, but Elmalılı rejects that reading: the looking is concurrent with the striking, not a state after death.
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r2.anchor: Birçokları bunu bakıp dururken yıldırım çarpmıştı, ölmüş idiniz mânasına anlamışlardır

ELMALILI:2:55-56/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r3.claim: He reads the looking clause as a circumstantial phrase or coordinated event concurrent with the striking; the parallel account calls the event a trembling calamity.
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r3.anchor: وَأَنتُمْ تَنظُرُونَ atfı veya hâli bilhassa böyle bir zehâba meydan vermemek içindir

ELMALILI:2:55-56/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r4.speaker: Vehb
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r4.claim: Vehb reports that they did not die: terror made them tremble so violently that their joints seemed to separate and their backs to break, bringing them near destruction.
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r4.anchor: Vehb hazretlerinden rivayeten dahi bunlar ölmemişler, belki o korkunç hâli gördükleri zaman kendilerini öyle bir titreme, bir zangırtı almış

ELMALILI:2:55-56/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r5.speaker: Vehb
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r5.claim: In Vehb's account Moses wept and prayed, God granted relief, and the people's senses returned; verse 56 describes their recovery as revival after death.
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r5.anchor: o zaman Hazret-i Mûsâ ağlamış, Rabbine dua etmiş, Cenâb-ı Allah da bir açıklık ihsan eylemiş

ELMALILI:2:55-56/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r6.claim: Two views place the event either after the killing episode or before it, immediately following the command; Elmalılı leaves the timing open.
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r6.anchor: Bu vâkı‘anın zikrolunan katlden sonra mı, veya ondan evvel ve katl emrini müte‘âkib mi olduğu hakkında iki kavil zikrediliyor

ELMALILI:2:55-56/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r7.claim: Whatever its timing, the calamity amounted to a people's death and their rescue to a renewed life and great blessing; the cause was refusing faith until they saw God, while release was divine care.
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r7.anchor: bu sâ‘ika bir kavmin memâtı mesâbesinde bir musibet

ELMALILI:2:55-56/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r8.claim: Although only a selected group of seventy at the meeting suffered the calamity, the Qur'an attributes the demand, trial, and revival to the whole people, including its later audience.
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r8.anchor: bizzat sâ‘ikaya tutulanlar da müntehab yetmiş kişi idi. Böyle olduğu hâlde bu âyette gerek dava, gerek musibet ve gerek ni‘met-i ba‘s

ELMALILI:2:55-56/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r9.claim: He explains the collective attribution through shared responsibility in public duties and communal obligations: the community, not an isolated individual, is the relevant subject, and all share its good and bad.
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r9.anchor: hukūkullah olan vezâif-i umûmiye mesâilinde, farz-ı kifâye maddelerinde ferd mevzû‘-i bahis değil, yalnız cemaat, nefs-i ümmet mevzû‘-i bahistir

ELMALILI:2:55-56/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r10.claim: After prior blessings, refusing Moses until seeing God was a grave act of disbelief and ingratitude, and the verse sharply warns about knowledge of God and human spiritual decline or ascent.
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r10.anchor: Hazret-i Mûsâ’ya isyan etmek ne büyük bir küfür ve küfrandır

ELMALILI:2:55-56/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r11.claim: Spiritual ascent frees sight, heart, and reason from the immediately visible and enables faith in unseen truths; decline narrows them to the senses and refuses anything not seen until disaster arrives.
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r11.anchor: insanlar terakki edecekleri zaman nazarları, kalbleri yükselir, idrakleri yalnız gözleri önünde duran mahsüsâta bağlanıp kalmaz

ELMALILI:2:55-56/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r12.claim: Sensory-only people want to touch and handle their deity; because worship is an innate human law, people unable to draw strength from the unseen seek tangible idols such as a calf.
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r12.anchor: Çünkü insanlarda ibadet kānûn-ı fıtrîdir. Bundan kurtulamazlar, fakat ma‘bûd-ı hakīkīyi göremeyince kalblerinden, akıllarından kuvvet alamayınca

ELMALILI:2:55-56/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r13.claim: Some Israelites, shaped by what they had seen in Egypt or their failure to rise spiritually, demanded that Moses show them God as a physical, encompassing object, an impossible demand.
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r13.anchor: veya herhangi bir sebeple tekrar sukūt etmiş olmaları dolayısıyla Hazret-i Mûsâ’ya

ELMALILI:2:55-56/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r14.claim: They treated God as if He were a bounded body before them, although such an encompassing vision was impossible; the miracles and evidence they had already seen should have sufficed.
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r14.anchor: bununla Allah’ı bir cisim gibi karşılarında muhît bir rü’yetle görmek istemişler ki muhal idi

ELMALILI:2:55-56/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r15.claim: The strike came as a miraculous punishment and the rescue as a miraculous act of mercy; though they did not see God, they saw a punishment no other deity could produce and learned the importance of faith without sight.
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r15.anchor: başka mâbudların yapamayacağı ‘ikābını görerek akılları başlarına gelmiş

ELMALILI:2:55-56/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r16.claim: God is not inherently unseen or impossible to see and can create eyes capable of seeing Him, but present eyes cannot bear Him and sight cannot encompass Him.
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r16.anchor: Lâkin ona bu gözler dayanmaz ve görülürse ihâta olunmaz

ELMALILI:2:55-56/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r17.claim: Human benefit in worldly life lies in believing in God while He is absent from sight, through rational and inward testimony.
ELMALILI:2:55-56/r17.anchor: Bizim dünyada fâidemiz ona gıyâbından şehâdet-i akliye ve kalbiye ile inanmaktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:49/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:49/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:49/r15.claim: This passage of al-Baqara summarizes the twenty-two verses on Israel's history in al-A'raf 7:141-162, while adding details about forgiveness after the calf, the demand to see God, the lightning, and revival.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:49/r15.anchor: Bakara sûresinin yukarıda meâli verilen kısmı, Hz. Mûsâ’nın hayatından, Kızıldeniz’i geçmesiyle başlayan bir kesit içermekte olup İsrâiloğulları’nın tarihine dair ayrıntılı bilgilerin yer aldığı A‘râf sûresindeki yirmi iki âyetin (141-162) tam bir özetidir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:49/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:49/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:49/r16.claim: After turning away again, the Israelites said they would not believe Moses until they openly saw God, and were struck down by lightning.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:49/r16.anchor: 55. âyette tekrar yoldan çıkarak, Allah’ı açıkça görmedikçe Mûsâ’ya inanmayacaklarını açıkladıkları, bu yüzden yıldırım felaketine uğratılarak yerle bir edildikleri

NAHHAS:v1p227/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p227/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p227/r2.claim: «جهرة» is a verbal noun functioning as a circumstantial; it means openly, without anything concealing the sight.
NAHHAS:v1p227/r2.anchor: ( جهرة ) مصدر في موضع الحال يقال رأيت الأمير جهارا أو جهرة

NAHHAS:v1p227/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p227/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p227/r3.claim: The idiom «يجاره بالمعاصي» describes someone who commits sins publicly, without hiding from people.
NAHHAS:v1p227/r3.anchor: ومنه فلان يجاره بالمعاصي أي لا يستتر من الناس

NAHHAS:v1p227/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p227/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p227/r4.claim: «الصاعقة» is nominative as the subject of its verb.

NAHHAS:v1p227/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p227/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p227/r5.claim: «وأنتم تنظرون» is a circumstantial clause, meaning “while looking.”
NAHHAS:v1p227/r5.anchor: ( وأنتم تنظرون ) في موضع الحال أي ناظرين

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p391/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p391/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p391/r1.claim: Here al-ṣāʿiqa means death; the next verse’s mention of their death supports this, as does the parallel in 39:68.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p391/r1.anchor: أحدها : الموت . ومنه قوله تعالى : ﴿ فأخذتكم الصاعقة ﴾ ، يعني : الموت ويدل عليه قوله تعالى

NASHR:v2p116/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p116/r3.speaker: أئمة الأداء
NASHR:v2p116/r3.claim: After an imāla rāʾ, as in نرى الله جهرة and وسيرى الله, the divine name’s lām may be heavy or light: one view notes no pure kasra before it, the other no pure fatḥa.
NASHR:v2p116/r3.anchor: إذا وقعت اللام من اسم الله تعالى بعد الراء الممالة في مذهب السوسي، وغيره كما تقدم

NASHR:v2p116/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p116/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو بن الحاجب
NASHR:v2p116/r4.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib prefers lightening the lām because its original state is light and neither a pure fatḥa nor ḍamma precedes it; he also reasons by comparison with a light rāʾ at pause. Ibn al-Jazarī accepts both performance variants.
NASHR:v2p116/r4.anchor: وقال الأستاذ أبو عمرو بن الحاجب إنه الأولى

NASHR:v2p77#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p77#2/r1.speaker: أبو القاسم الهذلي
NASHR:v2p77#2/r1.claim: Al-Hudhalī and other authorities report imāla from al-Sūsī through named routes; other routes preserve it for particular forms, including narā Allāh and sayarā Allāh.
NASHR:v2p77#2/r1.anchor: وقطع به أيضا للسوسي أبو القاسم الهذلي في كامله من طريق أبي عمران
